definition_zh: 溃烂；化脓；（情绪）积怨；恶化；腐烂
definition_en: to become infected and filled with pus, or to grow worse and more bitter over time
core_image: 伤口没有处理，脓水在里面慢慢积聚、发烫
scene: 小腿上的伤口一直没清理，几天后开始发热化脓。The cut on his leg was left uncleaned and began to fester within days.
sceneCN: 这里 fester 是「伤口化脓」（第 1 个义项：伤口感染并充满脓液）；句意：小腿上的伤口一直没清理，几天后开始发热化脓。

pos.zh: 溃烂；化脓；积怨；恶化；腐烂

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「化脓的；积怨难消的」
由过去分词转化的形容词，义为「已溃烂的；已积怨的」

senses.title: A wound filling with pus
senses.definition: (of a wound or sore) to become infected and produce pus
senses.definitionCN: （伤口或疮）感染并产生脓液
senses.example: The wound began to fester after the bandage was removed.
senses.exampleCN: 拆下绷带后，伤口开始化脓。
senses.why: Latin fistula named a pipe or an ulcer, and a sore that keeps leaking pus is the oldest picture behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fistula 本指管子或溃疡，不断流出脓液的疮口正是这个词最古老的画面。

senses.title: A feeling growing more bitter
senses.definition: (of an emotion or grievance) to become stronger and more bitter with time
senses.definitionCN: （情绪或怨气）随时间变得更强烈、更苦涩
senses.example: Resentment festered between the two brothers for years.
senses.exampleCN: 两兄弟之间的怨恨积压了很多年。
senses.why: The pus image moves from the body to the mind: what is never expressed keeps gathering and turns sour.
senses.whyCN: 脓液的画面从身体移到心里：从未说出口的东西不断积聚，最终变酸变苦。

senses.title: Being left to worsen
senses.definition: to be left untreated or ignored so that a problem grows worse
senses.definitionCN: 因未处理或被忽视而使问题变得更糟
senses.example: The dispute was allowed to fester instead of being settled.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端没有被解决，而是被搁置到不断恶化。
senses.why: A sore left alone does not stay still; neglect is exactly the condition that lets it spread.
senses.whyCN: 无人照管的疮口不会停在原处；忽视正是让它扩散的条件，所以「搁置」本身就带来恶化。

senses.title: Organic matter rotting
senses.definition: (of food, waste, or dead matter) to decay slowly with a bad smell
senses.definitionCN: （食物、废物或死亡有机物）缓慢腐烂并发出臭味
senses.example: Leaves festered in the stagnant water of the ditch.
senses.exampleCN: 树叶在沟里的死水中腐烂。
senses.why: Rotting matter and an infected wound share the same slow, smelly breakdown, so the word serves both.
senses.whyCN: 腐烂的有机物与感染的伤口共享同一种缓慢、发臭的崩解过程，因此同一个词可以兼指二者。

senses.title: A grievance gnawing at the mind
senses.definition: (of a remembered wrong) to stay in the mind and keep causing pain
senses.definitionCN: （被记住的委屈）留在心里并持续造成痛苦
senses.example: The old insult festered in her memory long after the argument ended.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵结束很久之后，那句旧日的侮辱仍在她记忆里隐隐作痛。
senses.why: An unhealed memory behaves like an unhealed sore: it throbs whenever something touches it.
senses.whyCN: 未愈的记忆就像未愈的疮口：一被触碰就会疼，所以积怨义项自然从伤口意象延伸出来。

senses.title: Corruption spreading quietly
senses.definition: (of an evil, a habit, or a bad practice) to spread and corrupt gradually
senses.definitionCN: （恶行、习惯或陋规）逐渐扩散并造成腐蚀
senses.example: Corruption festered inside the department for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 腐败在这个部门内部潜滋暗长了十年。
senses.why: Moral rot is imagined as an infection that spreads below the surface before it becomes visible.
senses.whyCN: 道德上的腐烂被想象成一种感染：先在表面之下扩散，等看见时已经深入。

senses.title: A sore point that will not heal
senses.titleCN: 未愈的心结；久拖不决的痛处
senses.definition: to remain as a painful, unresolved source of irritation
senses.definitionCN: 作为痛苦而未解决的刺激源持续存在
senses.example: The question of the inheritance festered for a generation.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产问题拖了一代人，始终是个未愈的痛处。
senses.why: The word keeps the physical sore in view: some matters stay tender and simply refuse to close.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始终保留着身体疮口的画面：有些事一直敏感，就是不肯愈合，于是有了「心结」的用法。

senses.title: A conflict getting worse
senses.definition: (of a quarrel or hostility) to become more intense and harder to settle
senses.definitionCN: （争吵或敌意）变得更激烈、更难平息
senses.example: Border clashes festered into a full-scale confrontation.
senses.exampleCN: 边境冲突不断加剧，最终演成全面对抗。
senses.why: The same growth from bad to worse gives the word its sense of a quarrel that will not cool.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「由坏走向更坏」的增长，让这个词也能表示一场不会降温的争吵。

intro.en: Fester comes through Old French festre from Latin fistula, a pipe or an ulcer; the discharging sore is the source of all its senses.
intro.cn: fester 经古法语 festre 上溯拉丁语 fistula（管子、瘘管或溃疡），不断排脓的疮口是它所有义项的源头。

items.en: Fistula means a pipe or a tube, and also an ulcer that keeps discharging.
items.cn: fistula 指管子、管道，也指不断排脓的溃疡。

items.en: Medical Latin uses fistula for an abnormal passage inside the body.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 fistula 指体内异常的通道，即瘘管。

items.en: Festre narrows the meaning to a sore or a fistula.
items.cn: festre 把词义收窄为脓疮或瘘管。

items.en: Fester first appears as a noun for a sore that discharges pus.
items.cn: 中古英语 fester 先作名词，指排脓的疮。

items.en: The verb sense of becoming infected and full of pus is recorded.
items.cn: 十六世纪记录了「感染并充满脓液」的动词义。

items.en: The figurative senses of bitterness, neglect, and slow decay become common.
items.cn: 积怨、搁置恶化与缓慢腐烂等比喻义在现代英语中通行。

note.en: Fester belongs to the sore-and-pus family; its neighbours are medical sore words and the vocabulary of grudges.
note.cn: fester 属于「疮口与脓液」词族，邻近的是医学上的疮口词和表示积怨的词汇。

entries.definition: an abnormal passage or an open sore
entries.definitionCN: 瘘管；开放性疮口；与 fester 同源

entries.definition: the process of becoming infected, or a bitterness that will not clear
entries.definitionCN: 化脓的过程；也指难以消解的积怨

entries.definition: a decorative chain of flowers or ribbons
entries.definitionCN: 花彩；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an open sore on the skin or inside the body
entries.definitionCN: 溃疡；皮肤或体内的开放性疮口

entries.definition: to cause lasting bitterness or resentment
entries.definitionCN: 使长期耿耿于怀；对应情绪上的 fester

entries.definition: to produce or discharge pus
entries.definitionCN: 化脓；医学用语，与伤口义项相近

normalIntro.en: Fester is a sore that will not close: the body, a grudge, or a quarrel keeps producing the same bad matter.
normalIntro.cn: fester 是一个不肯愈合的疮口：身体、怨恨或争端都在不断产出同样的坏东西。

normal.en: Fester and fistula are cousins: both name a channel that keeps draining.
normal.cn: fester 与 fistula 同源，都指不断排出的通道。

normal.en: A festering wound is one that will not close.
normal.cn: festering wound 就是不肯愈合的伤口。

normal.en: Resentment that is left alone will fester.
normal.cn: 无人理会的怨恨会不断积压。

normal.en: The word often appears with wound, resentment, and dispute.
normal.cn: 这个词常与伤口、怨恨、争端等词连用。

normal.en: Compare fester with rot: rot is for food, fester is for wounds and grudges.
normal.cn: 对比 rot：rot 多指食物腐烂，fester 多指伤口与积怨。

abstract.en: Picture a cut that stays warm and wet under a dirty bandage.
abstract.cn: 想象一处伤口在脏绷带下一直温热潮湿。

abstract.en: Imagine an old complaint letter that you keep rereading until the paper yellows.
abstract.cn: 想象一封旧日的控诉信，你反复读到纸张发黄。

abstract.en: Think of a garden gate left unpainted until the hinges seize.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇院门一直没人上漆，直到合页锈死。

examples.en: The cut on his hand festered because nobody cleaned it.
examples.cn: 他手上的伤口因为没人清理而化脓了。

examples.en: Old grievances festered until the two families stopped speaking.
examples.cn: 旧怨不断积压，最后两家人互不往来。

examples.en: Fallen fruit was left to fester at the bottom of the pool.
examples.cn: 落下的果子留在池底，慢慢腐烂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费事特」——伤口处理起来费事又特别麻烦，于是一直化脓；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fistula（管子、瘘管、溃疡）→ 古法语 festre（脓疮）→ 中古英语 fester（排脓的疮）→ 英语 fester，核心义「久不愈合、越拖越坏」。

sensesIntro.en: Fester starts with an infected wound, then extends to bitter feelings, neglected problems, rotting matter, and any conflict that grows worse.
sensesIntro.cn: fester 从感染的伤口出发，延伸到积压的怨气、被搁置而恶化的问题、腐烂的有机物，以及愈演愈烈的冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open sore that keeps leaking pus and will not close.
core.cn: 核心意象：一处敞开的疮口不断排出脓液，始终不肯愈合。

branches.en: The infected wound is the literal core of the word.
branches.cn: 感染的伤口是这个词字面意义上的核心。

branches.en: Bitterness that will not heal covers both a growing emotion and a remembered wrong.
branches.cn: 难以消解的苦涩既指不断增长的情绪，也指被记住的委屈。

branches.en: Neglect lets a sore or a quarrel grow worse.
branches.cn: 忽视会让疮口或争吵不断恶化。

branches.en: Rotting matter is the decay branch of the same image.
branches.cn: 有机物腐烂是同一意象中「腐烂」的分支。

branches.en: Quiet corruption and a lingering sore point both spread under the surface.
branches.cn: 悄然蔓延的腐败与久拖不决的痛处都在表面之下扩散。

intro.en: Fester is built on the Latin noun fistula, with English relatives such as festering, fistulous, and the older noun fester.
intro.cn: fester 建立在拉丁名词 fistula 之上，英语同族词包括 festering、fistulous 以及较早的名词 fester。

latinIntro.en: Latin fistula means a pipe or an ulcer; Old French festre narrows it to a discharging sore.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fistula 意为管子或溃疡，古法语 festre 把它收窄为排脓的疮。

items.exampleCN: fistula 是 fester 的直接拉丁语来源。

items.example: Festre carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: festre 把这个词带入法语。

items.meaning: to become infected and produce pus

items.exampleCN: 动词 fester 是日常使用的形式。

items.example: A festering wound needs cleaning.
items.exampleCN: 化脓的伤口需要清理。

items.example: The festered sore was slow to heal.
items.exampleCN: 已经溃烂的疮口愈合得很慢。

items.example: Fistulous belongs to the same medical family.
items.exampleCN: fistulous 属于同一个医学词族。

definition_zh: 脚镣；束缚；限制；禁锢
definition_en: a chain or shackle for the feet, or to restrain and limit someone or something
core_image: 一副铁环扣住脚踝，铁链拖在地上
scene: 囚犯脚上的铁链被解开，但他仍不敢走出那道门。The guard unlocked the fetter on his ankle, yet he still would not leave the cell.
sceneCN: 这里 fetter 是「脚镣」（第 1 个义项：锁住双脚的铁环与铁链）；句意：囚犯脚上的铁链被解开，但他仍不敢走出那道门。

derivatives.zh: 由 un- 加 fetter 构成，义为「解开镣铐；使自由」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「不受束缚的；自由的」
由 fetter 加 -less 构成，义为「没有镣铐的；无拘无束的」

senses.title: A shackle for the feet
senses.definition: a chain or metal ring fastened around the ankles to stop a person or animal from moving freely
senses.definitionCN: 锁在脚踝上、阻止人或动物自由行动的链条或金属环
senses.example: The prisoner wore iron fetters on both ankles.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯两只脚踝上都戴着铁脚镣。
senses.why: The oldest sense names the actual iron ring, because the word began as the object that holds the feet.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项指真实的铁环，因为这个词最初就是「扣住双脚的物件」本身。

senses.title: To chain someone by the ankles
senses.definition: to fasten fetters on a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 给人或动物戴上脚镣
senses.example: The guards fettered the runaway to a post.
senses.exampleCN: 看守把逃跑者锁在了一根柱子上。
senses.why: Once the noun names the iron, the verb naturally means putting that iron on someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然指那副铁具，动词自然就表示「把那副铁具戴到某人身上」。

senses.title: To restrain physically
senses.definition: to tie or hold a person or animal so that movement is difficult
senses.definitionCN: 把人或动物拴住、按住，使其难以行动
senses.example: They fettered the horse so it could not wander off.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把马拴住，免得它走失。
senses.why: The purpose of the ankle iron is restraint, so the verb extends from putting it on to restraining in general.
senses.whyCN: 脚镣的目的就是限制行动，因此动词从「上镣」扩展到一般的「拴住、限制」。

senses.title: To limit freedom
senses.definition: to restrict a person or group from acting or speaking freely
senses.definitionCN: 限制个人或群体自由行动或自由表达
senses.example: New laws fettered the press and silenced critics.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律限制了新闻界，让批评者噤声。
senses.why: An iron on the ankle becomes a picture for any rule or power that keeps people from moving freely.
senses.whyCN: 脚踝上的铁环成了任何阻止人自由行动的规则或权力的画面，于是生出「限制自由」的抽象义。

senses.title: To hold back progress
senses.definition: to slow or block the development of something
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物的发展变慢或受阻
senses.example: Heavy taxes fettered the growth of the small town.
senses.exampleCN: 沉重的税负阻碍了这座小镇的发展。
senses.why: If a chain can hold a body in place, it can also hold an economy or an idea in place.
senses.whyCN: 既然铁链能把身体固定住，它也就能把经济或想法固定在原处，于是表示「阻碍发展」。

senses.title: To bind by obligation
senses.definition: to make someone feel trapped by a duty, promise, or debt
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到被责任、承诺或债务困住
senses.example: He felt fettered by a promise he had made as a child.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得自己被儿时的一个承诺困住了。
senses.why: A chain need not be made of iron: an obligation can fasten a person just as firmly.
senses.whyCN: 锁链不一定由铁做成：一项义务同样能把人牢牢拴住，所以有了「受制于义务」的用法。

senses.title: Imprisonment or slavery
senses.definition: (in the plural) the state of being chained, imprisoned, or enslaved
senses.definitionCN: （常用复数）被铁链锁住、被囚禁或被奴役的状态
senses.example: The rebels were kept in fetters for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 叛乱者被戴上镣铐关押了三年。
senses.why: The plural fetters came to stand for the whole condition of captivity, not just the metal object.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式 fetters 逐渐代表整个被囚禁的处境，而不只是那件金属器具。

senses.title: To confine the mind
senses.definition: to stop the mind or imagination from developing freely
senses.definitionCN: 阻止思想或想象力自由发展
senses.example: Fear fettered her imagination and she wrote nothing for years.
senses.exampleCN: 恐惧禁锢了她的想象力，她多年写不出东西。
senses.why: The last step of the image is inward: what binds the body can also bind thought.
senses.whyCN: 这一意象的最后一步转向内心：能锁住身体的东西，也能锁住思想。

intro.en: Fetter is a Germanic word: Old English feter, a shackle for the feet, from Proto-Germanic fetur-; a link with the root of foot is often suggested but not certain.
intro.cn: fetter 是日耳曼语词：古英语 feter 指锁脚的镣铐，源自原始日耳曼语 fetur-；它与 foot 的词根联系常被提出，但并未证实。

items.en: The root ped- means foot; a connection with fetter is often suggested but not proved.
items.cn: 词根 ped- 意为脚；它与 fetter 的联系常被提出，但尚未证实。

items.en: Fetur names a shackle or a binding for the feet.
items.cn: fetur 指锁住双脚的镣铐或束缚物。

items.en: Feter and fetor mean a shackle or a chain for the feet.
items.cn: 古英语 feter 与 fetor 指脚镣或锁脚的链条。

items.en: Feter survives as the noun for ankle irons.
items.cn: 中古英语 feter 保留名词义，指脚踝上的铁具。

items.en: The verb fetheren appears with the sense of chaining by the feet.
items.cn: 十四世纪出现动词 fetheren，意为用镣铐锁脚。

items.en: Fetter extends from iron chains to any limit on freedom.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fetter 从铁链扩展到对自由的任何限制。

note.en: Fetter belongs to the Germanic family of binding words; its look-alikes are built with un- and -less, while its near meanings name other kinds of restraint.
note.cn: fetter 属于日耳曼语中表示「捆绑」的词族；形近词由 un- 与 -less 构成，近义词则指其他种类的束缚。

entries.definition: to free someone from chains or limits
without chains or restraint
entries.definitionCN: 没有镣铐的；无拘无束的

entries.definition: a part of the face, or a distinctive quality
entries.definitionCN: 面貌的一部分；特征；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a metal loop fastened around the wrist or ankle
entries.definitionCN: 手铐或脚镣上的金属环

entries.definition: a series of metal links used to bind or fasten
entries.definitionCN: 用于捆绑或固定的金属链

entries.definition: to hold someone back from acting

normalIntro.en: Fetter is an iron for the foot: the word starts at the ankle and ends by naming any limit on freedom.
normalIntro.cn: fetter 是套在脚上的铁具：这个词从脚踝出发，最后指一切对自由的限制。

normal.en: Fetter and foot begin alike, and the old word named the iron that held the foot.
normal.cn: fetter 与 foot 开头相近，这个古词本指扣住脚的铁具。

normal.en: Unfetter is to take the iron off, so the negated form is the one used for freedom.
normal.cn: unfetter 是把铁具取下，所以带否定前缀的形式反而用于表达自由。

normal.en: A fettered press is a press that cannot move freely.
normal.cn: fettered press 指无法自由运作的新闻界。

normal.en: Compare fetter with shackle: fetter is for the feet, shackle can be for wrist or ankle.
normal.cn: 对比 shackle：fetter 专指脚部，shackle 可指手腕或脚踝。

normal.en: The -ing form fettering often appears before nouns such as rules and regulations.
normal.cn: fettering 常出现在 rules、regulations 之类名词之前。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy iron ring closed around a thin ankle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的铁环扣在细瘦的脚踝上。

abstract.en: Imagine a key turning in a lock while the chain goes taut.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙在锁里转动，铁链随之绷紧。

abstract.en: Think of a horse tied to a post, circling a patch of bare earth.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹马被拴在木桩上，绕着光秃的土地打转。

examples.en: The prisoner was fettered to the wall of the cell.
examples.cn: 囚犯被锁在牢房的墙上。

examples.en: Rigid rules fettered the creativity of the young designers.
examples.cn: 僵硬的规则束缚了年轻设计师的创造力。

examples.en: The old lords kept their peasants in fetters.
examples.cn: 旧时的领主让农民戴着镣铐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费特」——戴上脚镣走路费劲，铁环又特别沉；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 feter（脚镣）→ 中古英语 feter → 英语 fetter；一般追溯到原始日耳曼语 fetur-（束缚双脚之物），与 foot 的词根联系存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Fetter moves from the iron ring itself to the act of putting it on, then to physical restraint, and finally to any limit on freedom, progress, duty, or thought.
sensesIntro.cn: fetter 从铁环本身出发，先指上镣的动作，再指身体上的拴缚，最后扩展到对自由、发展、义务与思想的限制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron ring closed around an ankle, with a chain dragging on the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只铁环扣住脚踝，铁链拖在地上。

branches.en: The iron ring is the literal object sense.
branches.cn: 铁环本身是字面意义上的器物义项。

branches.en: Putting the iron on and tying an animal both belong to the restraint branch.
branches.cn: 给人上镣与拴住动物都属于「束缚」这一分支。

branches.en: Limits on speech and limits on thought are the inward forms of the same chain.
branches.cn: 对言论与对思想的限制，是同一条锁链向内延伸的形式。

branches.en: A chain on the ground becomes a brake on growth.
branches.cn: 拖在地上的锁链变成对发展的刹车。

branches.en: Duty and captivity are two ways of being held without iron.
branches.cn: 义务与囚禁是两种不用铁链也能把人困住的方式。

intro.en: Fetter is a Germanic root word with English relatives such as unfetter, unfettered, and fetterless.
intro.cn: fetter 是日耳曼语词根词，英语同族词包括 unfetter、unfettered 与 fetterless。

latinIntro.en: Fetter has no Latin cognate; it belongs to the Germanic stock, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: fetter 没有拉丁同族词，属于日耳曼语来源，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: Feter is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: feter 是最早记录的形式。

items.example: The noun fetter names the iron itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词 fetter 指铁具本身。

items.example: The verb fetter is common in figurative use.
items.exampleCN: 动词 fetter 常见于比喻用法。

items.meaning: chains for the feet, or captivity
items.example: The plural fetters can mean captivity itself.
items.exampleCN: 复数 fetters 可以指囚禁状态本身。

items.example: A fettered mind cannot invent freely.
items.exampleCN: 受束缚的头脑无法自由创造。

items.meaning: the act of binding with chains
items.example: The fettering of prisoners was recorded in the log.
items.exampleCN: 给囚犯上镣铐的过程被记入日志。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unfetter.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unfetter。

items.example: Unfettered means without restraint.
items.exampleCN: unfettered 表示不受约束。

items.example: The suffix -less forms fetterless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 fetterless。

items.example: The suffix -less appears in fetterless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 出现在 fetterless 中。

definition_zh: 长期不和；世仇；宿怨；结怨
definition_en: a long and bitter quarrel, especially between families or groups, or to carry on such a quarrel
core_image: 两家人隔着院子怒目而视，仇恨一代代传下去
scene: 两个邻村为一块地争了几十年，仇恨代代相传。The two villages have feuded over a strip of land for generations.
sceneCN: 这里 feud 是「长期争斗」（第 3 个义项：动词，持续结怨）；句意：两个邻村为一块地争了几十年，仇恨代代相传。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成的名词，义为「长期的争斗；结怨」
由 blood 加 feud 构成的复合名词，义为「血仇；家族间的复仇性世仇」

senses.title: A long quarrel between families
senses.definition: a bitter quarrel between two families that lasts for a long time and is passed down
senses.definitionCN: 两个家族之间长期而激烈、还会传给后代的争斗
senses.example: The feud between the two families lasted for a hundred years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个家族的世仇延续了一百年。
senses.why: The core picture is inherited hostility, so the word first names a quarrel that outlives the people who began it.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是代代相传的敌意，所以这个词先指一场比发起者活得更久的争斗。

senses.title: Hostility between groups
senses.definition: a state of lasting hostility between communities, clans, or other groups
senses.definitionCN: 社区、宗族或其他群体之间持久的敌对状态
senses.example: A bitter feud divided the two communities for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 激烈的敌对让两个社区分裂了几十年。
senses.why: A family quarrel can grow into a group quarrel, so the same word covers whole communities.
senses.whyCN: 家族之间的争吵可以扩大为群体之间的争吵，因此同一个词也能指整个社区的对立。

senses.title: To carry on a feud
senses.definition: to keep up a bitter quarrel with someone over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 与某人长期保持激烈的争吵或敌对
senses.example: The neighbours have feuded over the boundary line for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两家邻居为边界线争了很多年。
senses.why: The noun names the quarrel, and the verb turns it into the ongoing act of carrying it on.
senses.whyCN: 名词指这场争斗本身，动词则把它变成「持续进行这场争斗」的动作。

senses.title: A dispute over land or rights
senses.definition: a long dispute about property, borders, or legal rights
senses.definitionCN: 围绕财产、边界或法定权利的长期争执
senses.example: The feud began as a quarrel about water rights.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宿怨最初是关于水权的争吵。
senses.why: Many inherited quarrels start with a concrete claim to land or water, which then hardens into a feud.
senses.whyCN: 许多世代相传的怨恨都始于对土地或水源的具体争夺，随后固化为世仇。

senses.title: A bitter public quarrel
senses.definition: a prolonged and public disagreement between prominent people or institutions
senses.definitionCN: 知名人物或机构之间长期而公开的分歧
senses.example: The mayor became involved in a public feud with the newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 市长与这家报纸陷入了一场公开的长期争执。
senses.why: The private family quarrel provides the model, and public life borrows it for disputes carried on in the open.
senses.whyCN: 私人的家族争斗提供了模板，公共生活借它来描述在众目睽睽之下进行的争执。

senses.title: A vendetta driven by revenge
senses.definition: a feud kept alive by the desire to punish a past wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因想要惩罚过去的伤害而延续的世仇
senses.example: His family carried on a feud with the men who had wronged them.
senses.exampleCN: 他的家族与曾经伤害过他们的人一直结着仇。
senses.why: When a feud is fed by revenge, it stops being a quarrel and becomes a vendetta, which is why the two words overlap.
senses.whyCN: 当世仇靠复仇来维持，它就不再只是争吵，而成了复仇行动，这也是这两个词意义重叠的原因。

senses.title: A long rivalry in sport or business
senses.definition: a prolonged and intense rivalry between teams, companies, or performers
senses.definitionCN: 球队、公司或表演者之间长期而激烈的竞争
senses.example: The two clubs have a long-running feud over young players.
senses.exampleCN: 这两家俱乐部为争夺年轻球员长期不和。
senses.why: The structure of a feud, two sides locked in repeated conflict, fits sport and business rivalries as well.
senses.whyCN: 世仇的结构是两方陷入反复冲突，这一结构同样适用于体育与商业竞争。

senses.title: A conflict that keeps flaring up
senses.definition: a conflict that seems to settle but breaks out again and again
senses.definitionCN: 看似平息却一次又一次爆发的冲突
senses.example: The feud flared again after the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选举之后，这场宿怨再次爆发。
senses.why: The word carries the idea of something long smouldering, so it suits conflicts that never quite end.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带有「长期闷烧」的意味，因此适合形容那些始终没有真正结束的冲突。

intro.en: Feud, a lasting quarrel, comes through Old French faide from the Germanic root faih-; it is not related to feudal, which comes from Latin feudum, a fief.
intro.cn: 表示长期争斗的 feud 经古法语 faide 上溯日耳曼语词根 faih-；它与 feudal 无关，后者来自拉丁语 feudum（封地）。

items.en: Faihitho names hostility, enmity, and a state of being at odds.
items.cn: faihitho 指敌意、仇怨以及彼此对立的状态。

items.en: Fah means hostile or outlawed, a cousin of the same root.
items.cn: 古英语 fah 意为怀有敌意的或被放逐的，是同词根的表亲。

items.en: Faide means enmity, a private war, or a vendetta.
items.cn: faide 意为敌意、私人战争或家族复仇。

items.en: Fede appears with the sense of hostility between families.
items.cn: 中古英语 fede 出现，指家族之间的敌意。

items.en: Feud settles into the sense of a lasting quarrel.
items.cn: 十五世纪 feud 定型为「持久的争吵」之义。

items.en: The verb use and the sporting rivalry sense develop.
items.cn: 动词用法以及体育竞争中的「长期不和」义随之发展出来。

note.en: Feud, foe, and feuding share a Germanic root meaning hostile; feudal looks similar but comes from Latin feudum, a fief.
note.cn: feud、foe 与 feuding 共享表示「敌对」的日耳曼语词根；feudal 形似，却来自拉丁语 feudum（封地）。

entries.definition: an enemy
the carrying on of a feud
relating to the feudal system of land and service
entries.definitionCN: 封建的；只是拼写相近，词源不同，源自拉丁 feudum（封地）

entries.definition: a long and bitter feud, especially one driven by revenge
entries.definitionCN: 家族血仇；尤指以复仇为动力的长期争斗

entries.definition: unfriendly opposition or strong dislike
an angry argument between people

normalIntro.en: Feud is hostility with a long memory: it begins as a quarrel and then lives on in children who were not there.
normalIntro.cn: feud 是一种记性很好的敌意：它始于一场争吵，然后活在并未亲历的下一代身上。

normal.en: Feud and foe share a Germanic root meaning hostile.
normal.cn: feud 与 foe 共享表示「敌对」的日耳曼语词根。

normal.en: A family feud passes from parents to children, which is why it lasts so long.
normal.cn: 家族世仇由父母传给孩子，这正是它持续如此之久的原因。

normal.en: Feuding is the noun for carrying the quarrel on.
normal.cn: feuding 是表示「持续争斗」的名词。

normal.en: Do not confuse feud with feudal: feudal land has a different Latin root.
normal.cn: 不要把 feud 与 feudal 混淆：feudal 的「封地」另有拉丁词根。

normal.en: A feud over water or land can outlive everyone who started it.
normal.cn: 为水源或土地结下的世仇，能比所有发起者活得都久。

abstract.en: Picture two farmhouses facing each other across a narrow lane, shutters closed.
abstract.cn: 想象两座农舍隔着一条窄巷相对，百叶窗紧闭。

abstract.en: Imagine children who have never met being told which family to hate.
abstract.cn: 想象从未谋面的孩子被告知该恨哪一家人。

abstract.en: Think of an offered handshake that is refused, again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一只伸出的手一次次被拒绝握住。

examples.en: The feud between the two villages began over a well.
examples.cn: 两个村子之间的世仇始于一口水井。

examples.en: The brothers feuded for years after the division of the farm.
examples.cn: 农场分割之后，兄弟俩争斗了很多年。

examples.en: Feuding neighbours finally signed a peace agreement.
examples.cn: 长期不和的邻居们终于签署了和平协议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费尤德」——两家人为一块地费尽口舌，怨气越结越深；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 faide（敌意、私战、家族复仇）→ 中古英语 fede（家族间的敌意）→ 英语 feud；一般追溯到原始日耳曼语 faihitho，与 foe 同源，与 feudal 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Feud begins with inherited family hostility, widens to groups and public life, adds the verb and the revenge-driven vendetta, and ends with rivalries and conflicts that keep returning.
sensesIntro.cn: feud 从代代相传的家族敌意出发，扩展到群体与公共生活，再加入动词用法和复仇性的宿怨，最后指长期竞争与反复爆发的冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two households glaring at each other across a yard, with the quarrel handed down to the next generation.
core.cn: 核心意象：两户人家隔着院子怒目而视，争斗被交给下一代。

branches.en: The inherited family quarrel is the central sense.
branches.cn: 代代相传的家族争斗是核心义项。

branches.en: Groups and land disputes widen the family quarrel into a public one.
branches.cn: 群体对立与土地争夺把家族争吵扩大为公共冲突。

branches.en: Carrying on the quarrel and long rivalry are the active forms of the same hostility.
branches.cn: 持续争斗与长期竞争是同一种敌意的行动形态。

branches.en: Public quarrels and recurring flare-ups show the feud in the open.
branches.cn: 公开争执与反复爆发让世仇暴露在明面上。

branches.en: Revenge is the fuel that keeps the feud alive.
branches.cn: 复仇是让世仇延续下去的燃料。

intro.en: Feud is a Germanic word borrowed through French; its English relatives include feuding and foe, while feudal is only a spelling neighbour.
intro.cn: feud 是经法语借入的日耳曼语词，英语同族词包括 feuding 与 foe；feudal 只是拼写相近的邻词。

latinIntro.en: Feud has no Latin cognate; its root is Germanic, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: feud 没有拉丁同族词，其词根属于日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: Faihitho is the reconstructed source noun.
items.exampleCN: faihitho 是重构出来的来源名词。

items.example: Fah is a cousin through the same root.
items.exampleCN: fah 经同一词根成为它的表亲。

items.example: Faide carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: faide 把这个词带入法语。

items.example: Fede is the Middle English form.
items.exampleCN: fede 是中古英语形式。

items.example: The noun feud names the quarrel.
items.exampleCN: 名词 feud 指这场争斗。

items.meaning: to carry on a lasting quarrel
items.example: The verb feud is common in journalism.
items.exampleCN: 动词 feud 常见于新闻报道。

items.meaning: the act of carrying on a feud
items.example: Feuding lasted for two generations.
items.exampleCN: 争斗持续了两代人。

items.example: Foe shares the hostile root.
items.exampleCN: foe 共享「敌对」这一词根。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms feuding.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 feuding。

definition_zh: 发烧的；发热的；狂热的；极度兴奋的
definition_en: having a fever, or showing the restless excitement of one
core_image: 额头滚烫、眼睛发亮，人在床上翻来覆去
scene: 孩子整夜额头发烫，嘴唇干裂，睡不安稳。The child was feverish all night, with dry lips and a restless sleep.
sceneCN: 这里 feverish 是「发烧的」（第 1 个义项：正在发烧）；句意：孩子整夜额头发烫，嘴唇干裂，睡不安稳。

pos.zh: 发烧的；发热的；狂热的；极度兴奋的

derivatives.zh: 由 feverish 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「发烧地；狂热地」
由 feverish 加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「发烧；狂热的状态」
由 fever 加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「发烧的；狂热的」

senses.title: Suffering from a fever
senses.definition: having a high body temperature caused by illness
senses.definitionCN: 因生病而体温升高、正在发烧
senses.example: She felt feverish and stayed in bed all day.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得发烧，在床上躺了一整天。
senses.why: The adjective is built directly on fever, so its first job is to describe a body that is running hot.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接由 fever 加后缀构成，所以它最初的任务就是描述一具「发烫」的身体。

senses.title: Showing the signs of fever
senses.definition: showing the physical signs of a fever, such as a racing pulse or dry skin
senses.definitionCN: 表现出脉搏加快、皮肤干燥等发烧的生理迹象
senses.example: The doctor noted his feverish pulse and dry skin.
senses.exampleCN: 医生注意到他脉搏加快、皮肤干燥，都是发烧的迹象。
senses.why: Once the word describes the illness, it can also label the symptoms that go with it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦能描述这种病，也就能标记随之而来的各种症状。

senses.title: Restlessly excited
senses.definition: extremely excited in a way that makes rest or calm impossible
senses.definitionCN: 极度兴奋，以致无法休息或平静下来
senses.example: The crowd grew feverish as the final whistle approached.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨声临近时，人群变得越来越狂热。
senses.why: A fever makes the body restless, and that restlessness is borrowed for excited crowds and minds.
senses.whyCN: 发烧让身体坐立不安，这种不安被借来形容兴奋的人群与头脑，于是有了「狂热」义。

senses.title: Frantically hurried
senses.definition: done in a frantic, hurried way, as if there is no time left
senses.definitionCN: 以慌乱的、赶时间的方式完成，仿佛已经没有时间
senses.example: There was a feverish rush to finish the report before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 大家慌慌张张地赶在午夜前完成报告。
senses.why: The heat of a fever becomes the heat of hurry: fast, uneven, and slightly out of control.
senses.whyCN: 发烧的热度变成匆忙的热度：快速、不均匀，而且有点失控。

senses.title: Marked by intense activity
senses.definition: full of intense and unusually fast activity
senses.definitionCN: 充满强烈而异常快速的活动
senses.example: The whole city was feverish with preparations for the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 整座城市都在为节日做准备，忙得热火朝天。
senses.why: A body in fever burns energy fast, and a place can be pictured as burning energy in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 发烧的身体快速消耗能量，一个地方也可以用同样的方式被想象成在快速消耗能量。

senses.title: Overwrought and unhealthy
senses.definition: excited in a way that seems unhealthy or too intense
senses.definitionCN: 兴奋得显得不健康或过于强烈
senses.example: His feverish imagination invented dangers everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 他病态般活跃的想象力到处制造危险。
senses.why: Not all heat is healthy: the word can suggest a mind burning too brightly, past the point of balance.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有的热都是健康的：这个词可以暗示头脑烧得过旺，已经越过平衡的界限。

senses.title: Flushed and hot in appearance
senses.definition: having a hot, flushed look on the skin
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤呈现出发烫、泛红的样子
senses.example: Her cheeks were feverish and her hands were cold.
senses.exampleCN: 她双颊发烫，双手却是冰凉的。
senses.why: Fever shows on the surface, so the word can describe the visible flush rather than the illness itself.
senses.whyCN: 发烧会显现在表面，因此这个词可以描述看得见的潮红，而不必指疾病本身。

senses.title: Filled with nervous anticipation
senses.definition: full of nervous eagerness while waiting for something
senses.definitionCN: 在等待某事时充满紧张而急切的期待
senses.example: He waited for the result with feverish impatience.
senses.exampleCN: 他焦灼不安地等着结果。
senses.why: Waiting can feel like a fever: hot, restless, and impossible to sit through calmly.
senses.whyCN: 等待可以像发烧一样：发烫、坐不住，无法平静地熬过去，于是有了「焦灼」义。

intro.en: Feverish joins fever, from Latin febris, to the Old English suffix -isc, meaning having the nature of.
intro.cn: feverish 由 fever（源自拉丁语 febris）加古英语后缀 -isc（意为「具有……性质」）构成。

items.en: Febris means fever, and febricitare means to be feverish.
items.cn: febris 意为发烧，febricitare 意为正在发烧。

items.en: Fefer and fefor name a fever.
items.cn: 古英语 fefer 与 fefor 指发烧。

items.en: The suffix -isc means having the nature of.
items.cn: 后缀 -isc 意为「具有……性质的」。

items.en: Fevrish appears as an adjective formed from fever.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 fevrish，是由 fever 构成的形容词。

items.en: Feverish extends from illness to excited and restless states.
items.cn: 十六世纪 feverish 从疾病义扩展到兴奋、躁动的状态。

items.en: The word now covers both a high temperature and frantic activity.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词既指体温升高，也指狂热的忙碌。

note.en: Feverish is fever plus -ish; its relatives are the fever word family, and its near meanings describe heat, restlessness, and hurry.
note.cn: feverish 是 fever 加 -ish 构成；它的同族词属于「发烧」词族，近义词则描述燥热、不安与匆忙。

entries.definition: an abnormally high body temperature
in a feverish or frantic way
relating to fever
entries.definitionCN: 发烧的；与发热有关的；与 feverish 同源

entries.definition: unable to stay still or calm
entries.definitionCN: 无法安静下来的；躁动不安的

entries.definition: wild with anxiety or rushed activity
entries.definitionCN: 因焦虑或匆忙而发狂的

entries.definition: red in the face, often from heat or exertion
entries.definitionCN: 脸发红的；常因发热或用力而泛红

normalIntro.en: Feverish is fever turned into a quality: a body, a crowd, or a schedule can all run hot.
normalIntro.cn: feverish 是把 fever 变成一种性质：身体、人群或日程都可以「发烫」。

normal.en: Feverish is fever plus -ish, so it literally means fever-like.
normal.cn: feverish 是 fever 加 -ish，字面意思就是「像发烧一样的」。

normal.en: Feel feverish is the everyday phrase for a rising temperature.
normal.cn: feel feverish 是体温升高时最日常的说法。

normal.en: Feverish activity is activity that runs hot and fast, like a fever.
normal.cn: feverish activity 指像发烧一样又热又快的活动。

normal.en: Compare febrile, the medical adjective from the same Latin noun.
normal.cn: 对比 febrile：它来自同一个拉丁名词，是医学用语。

normal.en: The suffix -ish turns a noun into a quality, as in childish and feverish.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ish 把名词变成一种性质，如 childish 与 feverish。

abstract.en: Picture a hand laid on a forehead and feeling the heat at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手放在额头上，立刻感到那股热度。

abstract.en: Imagine dry lips and bright eyes in a room that is too warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一间过热的房间里，干裂的嘴唇和发亮的眼睛。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd whose steps and voices keep getting faster.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人，脚步和说话声越来越快。

examples.en: She felt feverish and stayed in bed all day.
examples.cn: 她觉得发烧，在床上躺了一整天。

examples.en: The office was feverish with activity before the launch.
examples.cn: 发布之前，办公室里一片狂热的忙碌。

examples.en: He waited with feverish impatience for the letter to arrive.
examples.cn: 他焦灼不安地等着那封信到来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲沃瑞什」——额头滚烫、心里发慌，像有一团火在烧；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 febris（发烧）＋古英语后缀 -isc（……似的）→ 中古英语 fevrish → 英语 feverish，核心义「像发烧一样滚烫而不安」。

sensesIntro.en: Feverish begins with the body running hot, adds the symptoms and the visible flush, then transfers the same heat to excitement, hurry, intense activity, and nervous waiting.
sensesIntro.cn: feverish 从身体发烫出发，加入症状与可见的潮红，再把同一种热度转移到兴奋、匆忙、异常活跃与焦灼的等待上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hot forehead and bright eyes, with a body moving faster than it can bear.
core.cn: 核心意象：额头滚烫、眼睛发亮，身体动得比它能承受的更快。

branches.en: The illness and its symptoms are the literal medical branch.
branches.cn: 疾病本身及其症状是字面意义上的医学分支。

branches.en: Restless excitement is the first transfer from body to mood.
branches.cn: 躁动的兴奋是从身体转到情绪的第一步。

branches.en: Hurry and intense activity borrow the heat of the fever.
branches.cn: 匆忙与异常活跃借用了发烧的热度。

branches.en: Too much heat becomes an unhealthy, overwrought state.
branches.cn: 过热就变成一种不健康的、过度紧绷的状态。

branches.en: The visible flush and nervous waiting are the surface signs of the same heat.
branches.cn: 可见的潮红与焦灼的等待，是同一种热度表现在外的迹象。

intro.en: Feverish is built from fever plus -ish, with English relatives such as feverishly, feverishness, fevered, and febrile.
intro.cn: feverish 由 fever 加 -ish 构成，英语同族词包括 feverishly、feverishness、fevered 与 febrile。

latinIntro.en: Latin febris means fever, and febricitare means to be feverish; both feed the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 febris 意为发烧，febricitare 意为正在发烧，两者共同滋养了英语词族。

items.example: Febris is the Latin source of fever.
items.exampleCN: febris 是 fever 的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Febricitare lies behind the medical adjective febrile.
items.exampleCN: febricitare 是医学形容词 febrile 的来源。

items.example: Fever is the base noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: fever 是这个词族的基础名词。

items.meaning: affected by fever, or intensely excited
items.example: A fevered brow feels hot to the touch.
items.exampleCN: 发烧的额头摸上去是烫的。

items.meaning: having a fever, or restlessly excited
items.example: Feverish adds -ish to fever.
items.exampleCN: feverish 是 fever 加 -ish 构成。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms feverishly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 feverishly。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms feverishness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 feverishness。

items.example: The suffix -ish turns fever into feverish.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ish 把 fever 变成 feverish。

items.example: The prefix a- forms afebrile.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 a- 构成 afebrile。

items.example: Febrile is the medical counterpart of feverish.
items.exampleCN: febrile 是 feverish 的医学对应词。

latinEntries.example: Febris is the direct source noun.
latinEntries.exampleCN: febris 是直接的来源名词。
febricitare 提供了医学形容词的来源。

definition_zh: 易变的；无常的；不专一的；靠不住的
definition_en: likely to change suddenly and without warning, especially in loyalty, interest, or mood
core_image: 风向标随风一转再转，始终没有固定的方向
scene: 看台上的人刚才还在为这名球员欢呼，一次失误后就齐声嘘他。The crowd is fickle and turns on a player after one bad game.
sceneCN: 这里 fickle 是「易变的、不专一的」（第 1 个义项：喜爱或忠诚说变就变）；句意：人群是善变的，一场比赛没打好就转而攻击这名球员。

pos.zh: 易变的；无常的；不专一的

derivatives.zh: 由 fickle 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「善变；反复无常」
由 fickle 与 -minded 复合而成，义为「三心二意的」
由 fickle 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「善变地」，现代较少使用

senses.title: Loyalty that shifts
senses.definition: changing affection or loyalty often and without warning
senses.definitionCN: 感情或忠诚常常说变就变，事先没有征兆
senses.example: Fickle fans cheered the singer last week and booed her tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 善变的粉丝上周还为这位歌手欢呼，今晚就对她发出嘘声。
senses.why: Middle English fikel already meant not to be relied on, so affection that cannot be relied on became the first modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 fikel 已表示「靠不住」，所以「靠不住的感情」自然成为第一个现代义项。

senses.title: Weather that will not settle
senses.definition: changing often and unpredictably, as weather or luck does
senses.definitionCN: 像天气或运气那样频繁而难以预料地变化
senses.example: Fickle weather kept the fishing boats in port for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 变化无常的天气让渔船在港口停了三天。
senses.why: Old writers paired fickle with fortune and weather, the two things people can neither control nor predict.
senses.whyCN: 古代作家常把 fickle 与命运、天气搭配，因为这两样东西人既控制不了也预测不了。

senses.title: Taste that moves on
senses.definition: changing taste or preference quickly, so that the previous favourite is dropped
senses.definitionCN: 口味或喜好迅速改变，先前的偏爱很快被丢开
senses.example: Public taste is fickle, and a hit song can sound old within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 大众口味多变，一首热门歌曲一年之内就可能显得过时。
senses.why: Once the word meant unreliable in general, it attached easily to fashion and appetite, which change with the season.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦泛指「靠不住」，就很容易附到时尚与胃口上，因为它们跟着季节变。

intro.en: Fickle comes from Old English ficol, meaning deceitful or tricky; the modern sense of changeable grew in Middle English.
intro.cn: fickle 来自古英语 ficol，意为「欺诈的、狡猾的」；「易变」这一现代义在中古英语时期发展出来。

items.en: Ficol describes a person who is deceitful, cunning, or hard to trust.
items.cn: ficol 形容欺诈、狡猾、难以信任的人。

items.en: The related noun facen means deceit or treachery; the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 同族名词 facen 意为欺诈、背信；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Fikel drops the active idea of cheating and means unreliable or inconstant.
items.cn: fikel 丢掉了「主动行骗」的意思，转为「靠不住、反复无常」。

items.en: Writers apply fickle to fortune, weather, and lovers, all things that do not stay.
items.cn: 作家把 fickle 用于命运、天气和情人，这些都是留不住的东西。

items.en: Modern English keeps the word for loyalty, taste, and conditions that change fast.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这个词，用来指忠诚、口味和迅速变化的环境。

note.en: Fickle is the adjective of unreliable change, close to its own word family and to capricious and changeable.
note.cn: fickle 是表示「靠不住的变化」的形容词，与自己的词族以及 capricious、changeable 相邻。

entries.definition: the quality of being fickle
easily changing his or her mind
in a fickle manner
changing mood or behaviour suddenly
likely to change
changing quickly and unpredictably

normalIntro.en: Fickle began as a word for tricky people and now describes anything that will not stay the same.
normalIntro.cn: fickle 最初形容狡猾的人，现在形容任何留不住、定不下来的东西。

normal.en: Fickle weather is weather that cannot make up its mind.
normal.cn: 「fickle weather」就是拿不定主意的天气。

normal.en: Fickle fans leave a team as soon as it starts losing.
normal.cn: 「fickle fans」一看球队开始输就转身离开。

normal.en: Fickleness is the noun for the habit of changing.
normal.cn: fickleness 是表示「善变习惯」的名词。

normal.en: Old English ficol meant tricky, and a fickle person is still hard to pin down.
normal.cn: 古英语 ficol 意为狡猾，而一个 fickle 的人至今仍然让人摸不透。

normal.en: Compare changeable, which stays neutral, while fickle often carries blame.
normal.cn: 对比 changeable：它保持中性，而 fickle 常带责备意味。

abstract.en: Picture a fan swapping scarves at half time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个球迷在中场休息时换掉围巾。

abstract.en: Imagine a sunny sky dropping hail before lunch.
abstract.cn: 想象晴朗的天空在午饭前突然落下冰雹。

abstract.en: Think of a shop window redressed every Monday.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇商店橱窗每周一都重新布置。

examples.en: Fickle weather forced the crew to turn back.
examples.cn: 变化无常的天气迫使船员返航。

examples.en: Voters can be fickle, and one scandal may cost a party the election.
examples.cn: 选民可能很善变，一桩丑闻就可能让一个政党输掉选举。

examples.en: Her fickleness wore out the patience of every colleague.
examples.cn: 她的善变耗尽了每位同事的耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「非可」——说变就变，靠不住；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ficol（欺诈的、狡猾的），与 facen（欺诈）同族；中古英语 fikel 转为「靠不住、易变」，核心义是「无法依赖」。

sensesIntro.en: Fickle moves from something tricky and untrustworthy to loyalty that shifts, weather that will not settle, and taste that moves on.
sensesIntro.cn: fickle 从「狡猾、不可信」出发，长出「忠诚说变就变」「天气定不下来」「口味不断更新」三个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weather vane that turns with every gust.
core.cn: 核心意象：随风乱转的风向标。

branches.en: Affection that cannot be relied on is the personal sense.
branches.cn: 靠不住的感情是与人有关的义项。

branches.en: Weather and fortune supply the uncontrollable sense.
branches.cn: 天气与命运提供「无法控制」的义项。

branches.en: Fashion and appetite supply the taste sense.
branches.cn: 时尚与胃口提供「口味」义项。

branches.en: A fickle lover and fickle weather both refuse to stay the same.
branches.cn: 善变的情人与无常的天气都不肯保持不变。

branches.en: Weather and fashion both turn without warning.
branches.cn: 天气与时尚都会毫无预警地转向。

intro.en: Fickle is an Old English adjective with a small English family built on it.
intro.cn: fickle 是一个古英语形容词，英语围绕它构成了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Fickle has no Latin source: it descends from Old English ficol, and the deeper Germanic origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: fickle 没有拉丁语来源：它承自古英语 ficol，更早的日耳曼语来源不确定。

items.example: Ficol is the direct ancestor of fickle.
items.exampleCN: ficol 是 fickle 的直接前身。

items.example: Facen belongs to the same word family.
items.exampleCN: facen 属于同一个词族。

items.example: Fikel carries the word into Middle English.
items.exampleCN: fikel 把这个词带进中古英语。

items.example: Fickle keeps the modern sense of change.
items.exampleCN: fickle 保留「变化」的现代义。

items.example: Fickleness names the quality.
items.exampleCN: fickleness 指这种性质。

items.meaning: easily changing his or her mind
items.example: Fickle-minded combines fickle with minded.
items.exampleCN: fickle-minded 由 fickle 与 minded 复合。

items.example: Fickly is a rare adverb.
items.exampleCN: fickly 是较少用的副词。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms fickleness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 fickleness。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms fickly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 fickly。

items.meaning: having a stated kind of mind
items.example: The combining form -minded forms fickle-minded.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -minded 构成 fickle-minded。

definition_zh: 实地考察；田野调查；野外作业；（复数）野战工事
definition_en: research or practical work carried out in the real place being studied rather than in a library or laboratory
core_image: 研究者背着记录本走进村庄、山林或工地，在现场记下第一手材料
scene: 人类学学生在村子里住了一整年，跟着村民一起种地、过节、记账。The students did their fieldwork in a mountain village and filled twelve notebooks.
sceneCN: 这里 fieldwork 是「实地调查」（第 1 个义项：到研究对象所在的地方收集资料）；句意：学生们在山村做实地调查，写满了十二个笔记本。

pos.zh: 实地考察；田野调查；野外作业

derivatives.zh: 由 fieldwork 加 -er 构成，义为「实地调查员；野外工作者」
fieldwork 的前半部分，义为「田野；现场；领域」
fieldwork 的后半部分，义为「工作；劳动」

senses.title: Research in the real setting
senses.definition: the gathering of information by going to the place, group, or community being studied
senses.definitionCN: 走到被研究的地区、群体或社区去收集资料
senses.example: Her fieldwork among the fishermen produced a detailed account of their trade.
senses.exampleCN: 她在渔民中做的田野调查留下了一份关于这门行业的详细记录。
senses.why: Field first meant open land, so fieldwork is the work a researcher does out in the open instead of at a desk.
senses.whyCN: field 最初指开阔地，所以 fieldwork 就是研究者离开书桌、到外面去做的工作。

senses.title: Practical work done on site
senses.definition: practical work carried out on the spot, such as measuring, mapping, or testing
senses.definitionCN: 在现场进行的实际工作，例如测量、绘图或测试
senses.example: The geology students spent the morning on fieldwork along the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学学生上午在悬崖边做野外作业。
senses.why: Surveyors and engineers used the word for the outdoor half of a job, the half done in the field.
senses.whyCN: 测量员和工程师用这个词指一项工作中在户外完成的那一半，也就是在野外做的那一半。

senses.title: Earthworks built by troops
senses.definition: temporary fortifications thrown up by soldiers operating in the field
senses.definitionCN: 士兵在野外作战时临时修筑的防御工事
senses.example: The troops raised fieldworks on the ridge before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 部队在黎明前于山脊上筑起野战工事。
senses.why: In military use the field is the ground where an army operates, so fieldworks are the works built on that ground.
senses.whyCN: 在军事用法里，field 指军队活动的地面，所以 fieldworks 就是在这片地面上修筑的工事。

intro.en: Fieldwork is a compound of field, from Old English feld, open land, and work, from Old English weorc, labour.
intro.cn: fieldwork 是合成词：field 来自古英语 feld（开阔地），work 来自古英语 weorc（劳作）。

items.en: Feld means open land or plain, the ground not covered by forest.
items.cn: feld 意为开阔地、平原，即没有森林覆盖的地面。

items.en: Weorc means work, deed, or labour.
items.cn: weorc 意为工作、行为、劳作。

items.en: The two words are used together for labour done out on the land.
items.cn: 两个词开始连用，指在土地上做的劳作。

items.en: Fieldwork names the outdoor part of surveying and military engineering.
items.cn: fieldwork 指测量与军事工程中在户外完成的部分。

items.en: Social sciences borrow fieldwork for research done among people in their own setting.
items.cn: 社会科学借用 fieldwork，指在人们自己的生活环境里做的研究。

note.en: Fieldwork is the compound of field and work, close to its parts and to survey and expedition.
note.cn: fieldwork 是 field 与 work 的合成词，与两个组成部分以及 survey、expedition 相邻。

entries.definition: open land or an area of study
a person who carries out fieldwork
entries.definitionCN: 实地调查员；野外工作者

entries.definition: a short visit made by students to study something outside school
entries.definitionCN: 学生到校外考察的短途出行

entries.definition: a detailed study of an area or group
entries.definitionCN: 对某一地区或群体的详细调查

entries.definition: an organized journey made for study or exploration
entries.definitionCN: 为考察或探索而有组织地出行

entries.definition: a period of practical training in a workplace
entries.definitionCN: 在工作场所进行的实习期

normalIntro.en: Fieldwork simply joins field, the open land, and work, the labour: the labour of going out to the real place.
normalIntro.cn: fieldwork 就是把 field（田野）和 work（劳作）合在一起：到真实场所去做的活儿。

normal.en: Anthropologists do fieldwork by living among the people they study.
normal.cn: 人类学家住进被研究的人群中，以此做 fieldwork。

normal.en: Fieldwork notes are the raw records made on the spot.
normal.cn: 「fieldwork notes」就是在现场记下的原始材料。

normal.en: A fieldworker is the person who carries out fieldwork.
normal.cn: fieldworker 就是执行 fieldwork 的人。

normal.en: The fieldwork site is the place chosen for the study.
normal.cn: 「fieldwork site」就是为研究选定的地点。

normal.en: Compare survey, a close neighbour that often names the study rather than the staying.
normal.cn: 对比 survey：它常指研究本身，而不强调在那里住下来。

abstract.en: Picture a researcher with muddy boots and a notebook full of sketches.
abstract.cn: 想象一位研究者靴子沾泥，本子上全是速写。

abstract.en: Imagine a map being drawn on a clipboard while the wind blows.
abstract.cn: 想象风吹着，有人正把地图画在写字板上。

abstract.en: Think of a soldier piling stones into a low wall before sunrise.
abstract.cn: 想象士兵在日出前把石头垒成一道矮墙。

examples.en: Her fieldwork in the delta lasted eighteen months.
examples.cn: 她在三角洲的实地调查持续了十八个月。

examples.en: The course combines laboratory analysis with fieldwork in the hills.
examples.cn: 这门课程把实验室分析与山区的野外作业结合起来。

examples.en: Fieldworkers often face bad weather and long journeys.
examples.cn: 实地调查员常常要面对恶劣天气和长途跋涉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费尔德工作」——在 field（田野）里 work（干活），就是实地考察；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: field 来自古英语 feld（开阔地），work 来自古英语 weorc（劳作）；两个词合起来指「在野外进行的劳作」，核心义是「离开书桌，到现场去做」。

sensesIntro.en: Fieldwork starts as labour on open land, then narrows to research done on site, practical outdoor work, and finally military earthworks.
sensesIntro.cn: fieldwork 从「在开阔地上劳作」出发，收窄为到现场做的研究、户外的实际作业，最后指军队的野战工事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a researcher with muddy boots writing notes on site.
core.cn: 核心意象：靴子沾泥的研究者在现场做记录。

branches.en: Research among people in their own place is the academic sense.
branches.cn: 在人们自己的生活环境里做研究，是学术义项。

branches.en: Measuring and mapping outdoors is the practical sense.
branches.cn: 在户外测量与绘图，是实际作业义项。

branches.en: Earthworks built in the field are the military sense.
branches.cn: 在战场上修筑的工事，是军事义项。

branches.en: Both research and surveying leave the desk for the real place.
branches.cn: 研究与测量都要离开书桌，到真实场所去。

branches.en: Both practical work and earthworks are done on the ground.
branches.cn: 实际作业与工事都是在地面上完成的。

intro.en: Fieldwork is a transparent English compound, and its two parts still work as words of their own.
intro.cn: fieldwork 是一个构词透明的英语合成词，两个组成部分至今仍是独立的词。

latinIntro.en: Neither part of fieldwork is Latin: field and work both descend from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: fieldwork 的两个部分都不是拉丁语来源：field 与 work 都承自古英语。

items.example: Feld supplies the first part of fieldwork.
items.exampleCN: feld 提供 fieldwork 的前半部分。

items.example: Weorc supplies the second part.
items.exampleCN: weorc 提供后半部分。

items.meaning: open land or an area of study
items.example: Field keeps both the land and the study sense.
items.exampleCN: field 同时保留土地与研究领域两义。

items.example: Work names the labour in the compound.
items.exampleCN: work 指合成词中的劳动。

items.example: Fieldwork is the whole compound.
items.exampleCN: fieldwork 是完整的合成词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms fieldworker.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 fieldworker。

items.example: Field trip is a parallel compound.
items.exampleCN: field trip 是结构平行的合成词。

items.example: Field notes records what is seen.
items.exampleCN: field notes 记录现场所见。

items.meaningCN: 表示某一类工作的构词成分
items.example: The form -work also appears in homework and network.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -work 也出现在 homework 与 network 中。

definition_zh: 名义首脑；傀儡；挂名人物；船首像
definition_en: a person who leads a group in name only, or the carved figure fixed at the bow of a ship
core_image: 船头钉着一个人头木雕：位置最显眼，却管不了船往哪儿走
scene: 公司请一位退役将军挂名董事，真正的决定都由财务主管做出。The retired general is a figurehead; the finance director makes every real decision.
sceneCN: 这里 figurehead 是「名义首脑、傀儡」（第 1 个义项：看起来掌权、实际没有权力的人）；句意：这位退役将军只是个傀儡，每个真正的决定都由财务主管做出。

pos.zh: 名义首脑；傀儡；挂名人物；船首像

collocations.zh: 礼仪场合中的名义人物

derivatives.zh: figurehead 的前半部分，义为「形象；人物；数字」
与 figure 同源，义为「小雕像」
与 figure 同源，义为「比喻的」
figurehead 的后半部分，义为「头；首脑」

senses.title: A leader without power
senses.definition: a person who is officially the head of a group but has no real authority
senses.definitionCN: 名义上是某一群体的首领，却没有实际权力
senses.example: The king was a figurehead while the army governed the country.
senses.exampleCN: 国王只是个傀儡，治理国家的是军队。
senses.why: The carved head at the bow faces forward and looks important, yet it never touches the wheel.
senses.whyCN: 船首的木雕头像朝前，看上去很重要，却从不碰舵轮。

senses.title: The carved head on a ship
senses.definition: a carved figure, often a head or a whole body, fixed at the bow of a ship
senses.definitionCN: 钉在船头的雕刻形象，常为头像或全身像
senses.example: The figurehead of the old whaler was a painted mermaid.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘老捕鲸船的船首像是一个彩绘的美人鱼。
senses.why: Shipbuilders carved heads at the bow for luck and display, and the object took the name of its two parts, figure and head.
senses.whyCN: 造船者在船头雕刻头像，以求吉利和展示，这件东西便由 figure 与 head 两个部分组成名字。

senses.title: An empty post kept for show
senses.definition: a title or office that exists for ceremony or display rather than for power
senses.definitionCN: 为礼仪或摆设而设、并无实权的头衔或职位
senses.example: He was given a figurehead post with a desk and no staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他得到一个挂名职位，只有一张桌子，没有下属。
senses.why: Once the person was called a figurehead, the post that kept such a person was also called a figurehead post.
senses.whyCN: 当人被称作 figurehead 之后，供养这种人的职位也被叫作 figurehead post。

intro.en: Figurehead joins figure, from Latin figura, a shape, and head, from Old English hēafod; it first named the carved head at a ship bow.
intro.cn: figurehead 由 figure（源自拉丁语 figura，形状）和 head（古英语 hēafod，头）合成，最初指船首的木雕头像。

items.en: Figura means shape, form, or a figure made in some material.
items.cn: figura 意为形状、外形，或用某种材料做成的形象。

items.en: Figure passes from Latin into French as the shape or face of something.
items.cn: figure 从拉丁语进入法语，指某物的外形或面孔。

items.en: Hēafod means the head, and also the top or front of a thing.
items.cn: hēafod 意为头，也指某物的顶部或前端。

items.en: Figurehead names the carved head at the bow of a ship.
items.cn: figurehead 指船首雕刻的头像。

items.en: The word shifts to a leader who, like the carving, only decorates the front.
items.cn: 这个词转而指像木雕一样只装饰门面的领袖。

note.en: Figurehead joins figure and head, and its figurative sense stands close to puppet and mouthpiece.
note.cn: figurehead 由 figure 与 head 合成，其比喻义与 puppet、mouthpiece 相邻。

entries.definition: a shape, a person, or a number
a small carved or moulded figure
relating to figures or shapes
a person controlled by another
a person who speaks for an organization
a person used by another to do dull or dishonest work

normalIntro.en: A figurehead is literally a figure at the head of a ship, and the image of a decoration that cannot steer explains the modern sense.
normalIntro.cn: figurehead 字面就是船头的一个形象，而「装饰品不会掌舵」这一画面解释了它的现代义。

normal.en: A figurehead is a figure, a carved shape, fixed at the head, the front, of a ship.
normal.cn: figurehead 就是钉在船头（head）的一个雕刻形象（figure）。

normal.en: The carving looks like a captain but never steers.
normal.cn: 那尊木雕看起来像船长，却从不掌舵。

normal.en: A figurehead president signs what others have already decided.
normal.cn: 挂名总统只签署别人已经决定好的东西。

normal.en: Figurehead role and figurehead leader are the common collocations.
normal.cn: 「figurehead role」与「figurehead leader」是常见搭配。

normal.en: Compare puppet, which stresses being controlled, while figurehead stresses having no power.
normal.cn: 对比 puppet：它强调受人控制，而 figurehead 强调没有实权。

abstract.en: Imagine a captain hat on a man who never gives an order.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人戴着船长帽，却从不下达任何命令。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden head bolted to a bow, its eyes fixed ahead.
abstract.cn: 想象一个木头头像钉在船头，双眼直直望向前方。

abstract.en: Think of a nameplate on an office door with no one inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室门上挂着名牌，里面却空无一人。

examples.en: The chairman is a figurehead and the board decides everything.
examples.cn: 董事长只是个名义首脑，一切由董事会决定。

examples.en: The figurehead at the bow was carved from oak.
examples.cn: 船首的那尊雕像是用橡木雕成的。

examples.en: She was tired of being a figurehead and asked for real responsibility.
examples.cn: 她厌倦了当挂名人物，要求承担真正的责任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「figure 头」——船头挂着一个木头人，只是摆设；引申为有头衔、没实权的人。这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: figure 源自拉丁语 figura（形状、形象），head 源自古英语 hēafod（头）；合成词先指船首雕像，后引申为「只占前排、不掌实权的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Figurehead starts as the carved ornament at a ship bow, then becomes a leader who only decorates the front, and finally any empty post kept for show.
sensesIntro.cn: figurehead 从船首的雕刻装饰出发，转为只装饰门面的领袖，最后指任何为摆设而设的虚职。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carved wooden head at the bow that never touches the wheel.
core.cn: 核心意象：船首的木雕头像，从不碰舵轮。

branches.en: The powerless leader is the political sense.
branches.cn: 没有实权的领袖，是政治义项。

branches.en: The carving at the bow is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 船首的雕像，是字面义项。

branches.en: The post kept for show is the institutional sense.
branches.cn: 为摆设而设的职位，是制度层面的义项。

branches.en: The leader and the carving are both placed in front and both stay powerless.
branches.cn: 领袖与雕像都被摆在前排，也都没有实权。

branches.en: A nominal leader usually holds an empty title.
branches.cn: 名义领袖通常占着一个虚职。

intro.en: Figurehead is a compound of a Latin-derived noun and an Old English noun, and both halves are still common words.
intro.cn: figurehead 由拉丁语来源的名词与古英语名词合成，两半至今都是常用词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun figura means shape or form, and it comes from fingere, to form or fashion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 figura 意为形状、外形，源自动词 fingere（塑造、制作）。

items.example: Figura is the source of figure.
items.exampleCN: figura 是 figure 的来源。

items.example: Figure supplies the first half of figurehead.
items.exampleCN: figure 提供 figurehead 的前半部分。

items.example: Hēafod supplies the second half.
items.exampleCN: hēafod 提供后半部分。

items.meaning: the head or the front of a thing
items.example: Head keeps the body and front senses.
items.exampleCN: head 保留「头部」与「前端」两义。

items.meaning: a nominal leader or a ship carving
items.example: Figurehead is the whole compound.
items.exampleCN: figurehead 是完整的合成词。

items.example: The suffix -ine forms figurine.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ine 构成 figurine。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms figurative.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 figurative。

items.meaning: a person of a stated kind
items.meaningCN: 表示某一类人的构词成分
items.example: The form -head also appears in blockhead.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -head 也出现在 blockhead 中。

definition_zh: 电影制作；拍片；电影业
definition_en: the work of making films, from writing and shooting to editing and release
core_image: 一群人扛着摄影机、灯架和录音杆，把一个想法变成银幕上的画面
scene: 几个年轻人凑钱买了一台旧摄影机，决定自己拍一部短片。Their filmmaking began with a borrowed camera and a single street.
sceneCN: 这里 filmmaking 是「电影制作」（第 1 个义项：从写剧本到拍摄、剪辑的整个制作过程）；句意：他们的电影制作从一台借来的摄影机和一条街开始。

derivatives.zh: 由 filmmaking 去掉 -ing 并加 -er 构成，义为「电影制作人」
filmmaking 的前半部分，义为「电影；胶片」
由 film 加 -ic 构成，义为「电影的；电影般的」

senses.title: The making of a film
senses.definition: the whole process of writing, shooting, and editing a film
senses.definitionCN: 写剧本、拍摄与剪辑一部影片的整个过程
senses.example: Filmmaking takes months before a single scene reaches the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 在一个镜头出现在银幕之前，电影制作要花上好几个月。
senses.why: The compound simply joins film and making, so the word names the whole job of turning a script into a finished film.
senses.whyCN: 这个合成词就是把 film 与 making 拼在一起，所以它指把剧本变成成片的整套工作。

senses.title: The craft as an art or subject
senses.titleCN: 电影制作艺术；电影学科
senses.definition: the art and skill of directing and producing films, often studied or taught
senses.definitionCN: 执导与制片影片的艺术和技能，常被作为课程学习或教授
senses.example: She went to art school to study filmmaking.
senses.exampleCN: 她去艺术学校学习电影制作。
senses.why: Once the process was recognised as a craft, filmmaking became a subject with its own techniques and teachers.
senses.whyCN: 当制作过程被承认为一门手艺后，filmmaking 就成了有自身技巧和教师的学科。

senses.title: The film industry
senses.definition: the business of producing films for cinemas or streaming services
senses.definitionCN: 为影院或流媒体制作影片的产业
senses.example: Digital cameras opened filmmaking to people outside the big studios.
senses.exampleCN: 数码摄影机让大型制片厂之外的人也能进入电影业。
senses.why: The same word names not only the job but the industry that pays for it, since both are organised around making films.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指工作本身，也指为这项工作付钱的产业，因为两者都围绕制作影片组织起来。

intro.en: Filmmaking joins film, from Old English filmen, a thin skin or membrane, and making, from Old English macian, to make.
intro.cn: filmmaking 由 film（古英语 filmen，薄皮、薄膜）和 making（古英语 macian，制作）合成。

items.en: Filmen means a thin skin, membrane, or layer.
items.cn: filmen 意为薄皮、薄膜或薄层。

items.en: Macian means to make, form, or do.
items.cn: macian 意为制作、塑造或做。

items.en: Film is applied to the light-sensitive strip used in photography.
items.cn: film 开始指摄影用的感光胶片。

items.en: Film-making, often hyphenated, names the production of motion pictures.
items.cn: film-making 常带连字符，指电影的生产制作。

items.en: The spelling filmmaking settles as one word while the activity spreads to video and streaming.
items.cn: 随着这门活动扩展到视频与流媒体，拼写 filmmaking 固定为一个词。

note.en: Filmmaking is the compound of film and making, close to filmmaker and film-making, and to cinematography in meaning.
note.cn: filmmaking 是 film 与 making 的合成词，与 filmmaker、film-making 形近，与 cinematography 义近。

entries.definition: a person who makes films
a motion picture or a strip of photographic material
the making of films
entries.definitionCN: 电影制作，filmmaking 的连字符拼写

entries.definition: the art of filming images with a camera
the process of making a film or programme
the making of movies

normalIntro.en: Filmmaking is film plus making, and the word covers both the job and the industry built around it.
normalIntro.cn: filmmaking 就是 film 加 making，这个词既指制作工作，也指围绕它的产业。

normal.en: Filmmaking is film plus making: the making of a film.
normal.cn: filmmaking 就是 film 加 making：制作一部影片。

normal.en: A filmmaker is the person who does filmmaking.
normal.cn: filmmaker 就是从事 filmmaking 的人。

normal.en: Documentary filmmaking follows real people instead of invented plots.
normal.cn: 纪录片制作跟随真实的人，而不是虚构的情节。

normal.en: The filmmaking process runs from script to shoot to edit.
normal.cn: 电影制作过程从剧本到拍摄再到剪辑。

normal.en: Compare cinematography, which names the camera work inside filmmaking.
normal.cn: 对比 cinematography：它指电影制作内部的摄影工作。

abstract.en: Picture a camera crew squeezing into a narrow street at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象摄制组在黎明时挤进一条窄街。

abstract.en: Imagine a director watching the same ten seconds again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一位导演把同样的十秒钟看了一遍又一遍。

abstract.en: Think of a stack of film cans turning into a finished story.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞胶片盒最终变成一个完整的故事。

examples.en: Independent filmmaking rarely pays for itself.
examples.cn: 独立电影制作很少能收回成本。

examples.en: She taught filmmaking for ten years before directing her first feature.
examples.cn: 她教了十年电影制作，之后才执导自己的第一部长片。

examples.en: Digital filmmaking has lowered the cost of a first film.
examples.cn: 数字电影制作降低了一部处女作的成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「胶片 + 制作」——把胶片做成电影，就是电影制作；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: film 来自古英语 filmen（薄膜、薄皮），十九世纪转指感光胶片；making 来自 macian（制作）。合成词即「用胶片制作影像」，核心义是「把想法变成影片的全过程」。

sensesIntro.en: Filmmaking begins as the literal making of a film, grows into a craft that is studied, and finally names the industry that produces films.
sensesIntro.cn: filmmaking 先指字面意义上的「制作影片」，再成为一门可供学习的技艺，最后指生产影片的产业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crew with a camera turning an idea into images on a screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支带着摄影机的队伍，把一个想法变成银幕上的画面。

branches.en: The literal process of making a film is the first sense.
branches.cn: 字面上的制作过程，是第一个义项。

branches.en: The craft as a subject of study is the second sense.
branches.cn: 作为学习对象的技艺，是第二个义项。

branches.en: The industry that pays for films is the third sense.
branches.cn: 为影片出资的产业，是第三个义项。

branches.en: The process and the craft are the same work seen from practice and from study.
branches.cn: 制作过程与制作技艺是同一件事，分别从实践和学习的角度看。

branches.en: The process and the industry both exist because films must be made.
branches.cn: 制作过程与电影业都存在，因为影片必须被制作出来。

intro.en: Filmmaking is a native English compound of film and making, and the suffix -ing turns the verb make into a noun of action.
intro.cn: filmmaking 是英语本土合成词，由 film 与 making 组成，后缀 -ing 把动词 make 变成表示动作的名词。

latinIntro.en: Filmmaking has no Latin source: film and make both come from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: filmmaking 没有拉丁语来源：film 与 make 都来自古英语。

items.example: Filmen is the ancestor of film.
items.exampleCN: filmen 是 film 的前身。

items.meaning: a thin layer, photographic film, or a movie
items.example: Film supplies the first half of filmmaking.
items.exampleCN: film 提供 filmmaking 的前半部分。

items.example: Macian is the ancestor of make.
items.exampleCN: macian 是 make 的前身。

items.example: Make supplies the verb behind making.
items.exampleCN: make 是 making 背后的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms making.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 making。

items.example: Filmmaking is the whole compound.
items.exampleCN: filmmaking 是完整的合成词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms filmmaker.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 filmmaker。

items.example: Film-making is an older spelling.
items.exampleCN: film-making 是较早的拼写。

definition_zh: 终曲；终场；大结局；季终集
definition_en: the last part of a piece of music, a stage show, or a series, often the most exciting part
core_image: 舞台灯光渐暗，最后一个和弦落下
scene: 演出接近尾声，全场观众都在等待最后的终曲。As the concert drew to a close, the whole hall waited for the grand finale.
sceneCN: 这里 finale 是「终曲、终场」（第 1 个义项：音乐作品或演出最后的段落）；句意：音乐会接近尾声，全场都在等待盛大的终曲。

derivatives.zh: 同出拉丁语词根 finis，义为「最后的」
final 加 -ly 构成，义为「最后；终于」
final 加 -ist 构成，义为「进入决赛的选手」
final 加 -ize 构成，义为「最终确定；定稿」

senses.title: The closing section of a piece of music
senses.definition: the last movement or passage of a musical work
senses.definitionCN: 音乐作品最后的乐章或段落
senses.example: The symphony ends with a slow finale.
senses.exampleCN: 这部交响曲以一个缓慢的终曲结束。
senses.why: In Italian the word simply means final, so musicians used it for the closing part of a work.
senses.whyCN: 在意大利语里这个词就是「最后的」，乐师便用它称呼作品的收尾段落。

senses.title: The last act of a stage show
senses.definition: the concluding act or scene of an opera, a ballet, or a stage show
senses.definitionCN: 歌剧、芭蕾或舞台演出结束时的最后一幕
senses.example: The opera builds to a fiery finale.
senses.exampleCN: 这部歌剧在炽烈的末幕中达到高潮。
senses.why: Stage works borrowed the musical term for the scene that closes the evening.
senses.whyCN: 舞台作品借用了音乐术语，用来指为整晚演出收尾的一幕。

senses.title: The last episode of a television season
senses.definition: the last episode of a season or of a whole television series
senses.definitionCN: 一季或整部电视剧的最后一集
senses.example: Viewers waited all year for the season finale.
senses.exampleCN: 观众等了一整年才看到这一季的终集。
senses.why: Television lifted the concert word for the episode that closes a season.
senses.whyCN: 电视业借用了音乐会用语，指为一季收尾的那一集。

senses.title: A spectacular ending to an event
senses.definition: an exciting or impressive end to an event or a period
senses.definitionCN: 事件或时期令人激动、印象深刻的结束
senses.example: The festival closed with a fireworks finale.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节以一场烟花收尾。
senses.why: Because the musical finale is the most spectacular part, the word came to mean any impressive ending.
senses.whyCN: 音乐的终曲最为华彩，于是这个词也指任何令人惊叹的结束。

senses.title: The last stage of a process
senses.definition: the final stage of a process, a period, or a sequence of events
senses.definitionCN: 过程、时期或事件序列的最后阶段
senses.example: The finale of the negotiation was a quiet handshake.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判的收尾是一次安静的握手。
senses.why: The sense widens from art to any sequence that reaches its end.
senses.whyCN: 词义从艺术领域扩展到任何走向终点的序列。

intro.en: Finale is Italian for final; English took it from the opera house, where it names the closing number.
intro.cn: finale 是意大利语中「最后的」一词，英语从歌剧院借来，用来指收场的段落。

items.en: Finis means a boundary or an end.
items.cn: finis 意为边界或终点。

items.en: Finalis means of the end, or last.
items.cn: finalis 意为「末尾的、最后的」。

items.en: Finale is the adjective used as a noun for the closing part of a work.
items.cn: finale 是形容词作名词用，指作品的收尾部分。

items.en: Opera composers label the last number of a work the finale.
items.cn: 歌剧作曲家把作品的最后一曲标为 finale。

items.en: English borrows finale as a term of music and theatre.
items.cn: 英语把 finale 借入，作为音乐与戏剧术语。

items.en: The word spreads to television seasons and to any grand ending.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到电视剧的季终集以及任何盛大收尾。

note.en: Finale shares the Latin root finis with final and finalist, and sits close to the ordinary words for an ending.
note.cn: finale 与 final、finalist 共享拉丁语词根 finis，并与表示「结尾」的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: coming at the end; last
a competitor who reaches the last round
to put something into its final form
the last part of a story or an event
the most intense point of a story or an event
the end or finish of something

normalIntro.en: Finale is the last page of the score, the moment the lights go down.
normalIntro.cn: finale 是乐谱的最后一页，也是灯光暗下来的那一刻。

normal.en: Grand finale is the big closing number of a show.
normal.cn: grand finale 是演出最盛大的收场节目。

normal.en: A season finale ends one year of a television series.
normal.cn: season finale 为电视剧的一季收尾。

normal.en: The Italian word finale simply means final.
normal.cn: 意大利语 finale 的意思就是「最后的」。

normal.en: Final and finally share the same Latin root finis.
normal.cn: final 与 finally 共享拉丁词根 finis。

normal.en: Use finale for art and spectacle, and ending for ordinary things.
normal.cn: finale 多用于艺术与盛大场面，平常事物用 ending。

abstract.en: Hear the orchestra tighten into one last chord.
abstract.cn: 想象乐队收拢成最后一个和弦。

abstract.en: See the curtain fall on the last scene of an opera.
abstract.cn: 想象歌剧最后一幕的幕布落下。

abstract.en: Picture a television screen fading to black after the last episode.
abstract.cn: 想象最后一集播完后电视屏幕渐渐变黑。

examples.en: The pianist ended the recital with a brilliant finale.
examples.cn: 钢琴家以一段辉煌的终曲结束了独奏会。

examples.en: Fans debated the season finale for weeks.
examples.cn: 粉丝们为这一季的终集争论了好几周。

examples.en: The fireworks served as the finale of the evening.
examples.cn: 烟花成了那个夜晚的收尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲纳利」——听起来像谢幕时被念出的名字，提示这是演出的收尾；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 意大利语 finale（最后的）← 拉丁语 finalis（末尾的）← finis（终点、边界）→ 英语 finale，核心义「抵达终点的那一段」。

sensesIntro.en: Finale starts as the closing number of a musical work, moves to the last act of a show and the last episode of a season, and then widens to any impressive end.
sensesIntro.cn: finale 从乐曲的末段开始，转到演出的末幕与一季的最后一集，再扩展到任何令人印象深刻的收尾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last chord sounding as the lights dim.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯光渐暗时落下的最后一个和弦。

branches.en: The musical close is the source sense.
branches.cn: 乐曲的收尾是最初的义项。

branches.en: The last act of a stage work extends the musical term.
branches.cn: 舞台作品的末幕是音乐术语的延伸。

branches.en: Television borrows the word for its season ending.
branches.cn: 电视借用这个词指一季的结束。

branches.en: Both the score and the fireworks end on a designed high point.
branches.cn: 乐谱与烟花都以设计好的高点收束。

branches.en: Any event or process can now have its own finale.
branches.cn: 任何事件或过程现在都可以有自己的收尾。

intro.en: Finale is an Italian borrowing built on Latin finis, and English forms final, finally, finalist, and finalize around the same root.
intro.cn: finale 是建立在拉丁语 finis 之上的意大利语借词，英语围绕同一词根构成 final、finally、finalist 与 finalize。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis means end or boundary, and finalis means last; Italian turned the adjective into a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 意为终点或边界，finalis 意为最后的；意大利语把这个形容词用作了名词。

items.example: Finis supplies the core idea of an end.
items.exampleCN: finis 提供「终点」这一核心义。

items.example: Finalis is the adjective behind finale.
items.exampleCN: finalis 是 finale 背后的形容词。

items.meaning: the closing part of a work
items.example: Italian finale names the last number of a score.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语 finale 指乐谱的最后一曲。

items.example: English final came from the same Latin adjective.
items.exampleCN: 英语 final 来自同一个拉丁形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns final into finally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 把 final 变成 finally。

items.example: Finally marks the point where something ends.
items.exampleCN: finally 标记某事结束的那一刻。

items.meaning: a person who does or reaches
items.meaningCN: 从事或达到某境地的人
items.example: The suffix -ist forms finalist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 finalist。

items.meaning: a person in the last round
items.example: Finalist adds a person to the adjective final.
items.exampleCN: finalist 在形容词 final 之上加出一个人。

items.example: The suffix -ize builds the verb finalize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成动词 finalize。

items.example: Finalize turns the adjective into an action.
items.exampleCN: finalize 把形容词变成动作。

definition_zh: 雀；小型雀类；食籽小鸟
definition_en: a small songbird with a short, strong beak, usually feeding on seeds
core_image: 一只小雀用短喙磕开草籽的硬壳
scene: 清晨的草丛里，一只小雀一边跳跃一边找草籽。At dawn a little finch hopped through the grass, cracking seeds with its short beak.
sceneCN: 这里 finch 是「雀」这一鸟类（第 1 个义项：小型食籽鸣禽）；句意：天刚亮，一只小雀在草丛里跳跃，用短喙磕开种子。

collocations.zh: 斑胸草雀（常用的实验鸟）

derivatives.zh: 由 gold 与 finch 复合而成，指羽色鲜黄的金翅雀
由 chaff 与 finch 复合而成，指欧洲常见的苍头燕雀
由 bull 与 finch 复合而成，指体型敦实的红腹灰雀

senses.title: A small seed-eating songbird
senses.definition: any of many small songbirds with short, stout beaks that crack seeds
senses.definitionCN: 多种喙短而粗壮、能磕开种子的小型鸣禽
senses.example: A finch perched on the garden wall.
senses.exampleCN: 一只雀停在花园的墙头上。
senses.why: The Germanic name was probably coined from the call of the bird, so the word begins as the bird itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个日耳曼语名称很可能取自鸟本身的叫声，所以词一开始就是指这种鸟。

senses.title: A bird of the true finch family
senses.definition: a bird belonging to the family that includes chaffinches and goldfinches
senses.definitionCN: 属于包含苍头燕雀与金翅雀的那一科的鸟
senses.example: Chaffinches and goldfinches are true finches.
senses.exampleCN: 苍头燕雀与金翅雀都是真正的雀科鸟类。
senses.why: Bird scientists fixed the everyday name onto one family, so finch became a taxonomic label.
senses.whyCN: 鸟类学家把这个日常称呼固定到一个科上，finch 于是成了分类学标签。

senses.title: A bird of the estrildid group
senses.definition: a small seed-eating bird of the waxbill group, such as the zebra finch
senses.definitionCN: 梅花雀一类的小型食籽鸟，如斑胸草雀
senses.example: The zebra finch is an estrildid finch from Australia.
senses.exampleCN: 斑胸草雀是来自澳洲的一种梅花雀类。
senses.why: Because the name described a habit rather than a family, it easily covered similar birds in other groups.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名称描述的是习性而非血统，它很容易也覆盖其他类群中相似的鸟。

senses.title: A cage bird kept for its song
senses.definition: a finch bred and kept in a cage for its song or its colours
senses.definitionCN: 为听鸣唱或观羽色而饲养在笼中的雀
senses.example: He keeps a finch in a cage by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他在窗边养了一只雀。
senses.why: Small size and quick song made finches the classic cage bird, adding a domestic sense to the name.
senses.whyCN: 体型小巧、鸣声轻快，使雀成为典型的笼鸟，名称因此多了家养的含义。

senses.title: A laboratory model for song learning
senses.definition: a finch used in research on how birds learn and produce song, especially the zebra finch
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究鸟类如何学习与发出鸣唱的实验雀，尤指斑胸草雀
senses.example: The lab raised finches to study vocal learning.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室饲养雀类以研究发声学习。
senses.why: One species became a standard subject, so the plain bird name now also labels a research animal.
senses.whyCN: 其中一个物种成了标准实验对象，这个普通的鸟名于是也指实验动物。

intro.en: Finch is a Germanic bird name, with no Latin source, and it is probably echoic of the call of the bird.
intro.cn: finch 是日耳曼语的鸟名，没有拉丁语来源，很可能模仿鸟的叫声。

items.en: A reconstructed word such as finko or finkiz named the bird, probably from its note.
items.cn: 重构形式 finko 或 finkiz 指这种鸟，可能来自它的叫声。

items.en: Old English records finc for the small seed-eating bird.
items.cn: 古英语以 finc 记录这种小型食籽鸟。

items.en: Old High German finko is the cognate that confirms the shared Germanic source.
items.cn: 古高地德语 finko 是同源词，印证了共同的日耳曼语来源。

items.en: Middle English settles on the spelling finch.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写固定为 finch。

items.en: Modern English builds compound names such as goldfinch and chaffinch.
items.cn: 现代英语构成 goldfinch、chaffinch 等复合鸟名。

items.en: The zebra finch becomes a standard laboratory bird for the study of song.
items.cn: 斑胸草雀成为研究鸣唱的标准实验鸟。

note.en: Finch is the base of many compound bird names and stands close to other small seed-eating birds.
note.cn: finch 是许多复合鸟名的基干，并与其它小型食籽鸟相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 欧洲常见的雀，胸前呈粉色

entries.definition: a finch with bright yellow wing patches

normal.en: A finch cracks seeds with a short, strong beak.
normal.cn: 雀用短而有力的喙磕开种子。

normal.en: Goldfinch and chaffinch are compound finch names.
normal.cn: goldfinch 与 chaffinch 都是带 finch 的复合鸟名。

normal.en: The zebra finch is a favourite laboratory bird.
