normal.en: German Fink and Dutch vink are cognates of finch.
normal.cn: 德语 Fink 与荷兰语 vink 都是 finch 的同源词。

normal.en: Finches belong to the seed-eating branch of songbirds.
normal.cn: 雀类属于鸣禽中吃种子的一支。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny beak prying a seed shell apart.
abstract.cn: 想象一张小喙把种壳撬开。

abstract.en: See a flock of chaffinches on a winter hedge.
abstract.cn: 想象冬日树篱上的一群苍头燕雀。

abstract.en: Watch a zebra finch sing its practised phrase.
abstract.cn: 想象一只斑胸草雀唱出练熟的短句。

examples.en: A finch sang from the top of the hedge.
examples.cn: 一只雀在树篱顶上鸣唱。

examples.en: The zoo keeps several finches in a planted aviary.
examples.cn: 动物园在一个种了植物的鸟舍里养着几只雀。

examples.en: Researchers study how the zebra finch learns its song.
examples.cn: 研究者研究斑胸草雀如何学会鸣唱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「芬奇」——读音近似那位画家的名字，好记又好玩，指一种小鸟；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始日耳曼语 finko（可能模仿鸟鸣）→ 古英语 finc → 中古英语 finch → 英语 finch，核心义「会磕种子的短喙小鸟」。

sensesIntro.en: Finch begins as the everyday name of a seed-eating songbird, then narrows to the true finch family and to the estrildid group, and finally reaches the cage and the laboratory.
sensesIntro.cn: finch 起初是这类食籽鸣禽的日常称呼，随后分别指向雀科与梅花雀类，最后进入鸟笼与实验室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small beak splitting a seed shell.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张小喙撬开种壳。

branches.en: The everyday bird is the source sense.
branches.cn: 日常所说的这种鸟是最初的义项。

branches.en: The everyday name was pinned onto one scientific family.
branches.cn: 日常名称被固定到某一个科上。

branches.en: Two families of seed eaters both carry the name.
branches.cn: 两个食籽的类群都带着这个名称。

branches.en: The small size that suits a cage also suits the songbird trade.
branches.cn: 适合入笼的小巧体型也适合鸣禽买卖。

branches.en: One estrildid species became the standard research bird.
branches.cn: 一种梅花雀类成了标准的实验鸟。

intro.en: Finch is a Germanic bird name with no Latin source; its English family grows by compounding, as in goldfinch and chaffinch.
intro.cn: finch 是日耳曼语鸟名，没有拉丁语来源；它在英语中的词族靠复合成词扩展，如 goldfinch 与 chaffinch。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate for finch, so the Latin list is empty; the bird name belongs to the Germanic group.
latinIntro.cn: finch 没有拉丁语同源词，所以拉丁同源词一栏留空；这个鸟名属于日耳曼语族。

items.example: Finch is the base name of the family.
items.exampleCN: finch 是这一词族的基干名称。

items.meaning: plural ending after ch, sh, and s
items.meaningCN: 接在 ch、sh、s 之后的复数词尾
items.example: The ending -es makes finches easy to say.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -es 让 finches 读起来顺口。

items.example: Finches adds the plural ending to the noun.
items.exampleCN: finches 给名词加上复数词尾。

items.example: Goldfinch names a brightly coloured finch.
items.exampleCN: goldfinch 指羽色鲜亮的雀。

items.example: Chaffinch is a common European finch.
items.exampleCN: chaffinch 是欧洲常见的雀。

items.example: Greenfinch names a green-plumaged bird.
items.exampleCN: greenfinch 指羽色发绿的雀。

items.example: Bullfinch names a stout finch.
items.exampleCN: bullfinch 指体型敦实的雀。

items.meaning: zebra plus finch, a striped Australian bird
items.meaningCN: 斑马纹与雀复合，指澳洲的斑胸草雀
items.example: Zebra finch is the laboratory songbird.
items.exampleCN: zebra finch 就是实验室里那种鸣禽。

definition_zh: 指纹；指纹印；取指纹；独特印记
definition_en: the mark left by the ridges of a finger, or a unique pattern that identifies a person or a thing
core_image: 指尖按在玻璃上，留下一圈圈螺纹
scene: 警员让嫌疑人在卡片上按下自己的指印。The officer asked the suspect to press a fingerprint onto the card.
sceneCN: 这里 fingerprint 是「指纹印」（第 1 个义项：手指留下的印痕）；句意：警员让嫌疑人在卡片上按下指纹。

collocations.zh: 潜在指纹（留在现场、需显影的指纹）

derivatives.zh: 动词 fingerprint 加 -ing 构成，义为「指纹采集；指纹鉴定」
fingerprint 与 scanner 复合而成，义为「指纹扫描仪」
fingerprint 与 reader 复合而成，义为「指纹读取器」

senses.title: The mark left by a finger
senses.definition: the visible mark that the ridges of a finger leave on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 手指的纹路在表面上留下的可见印痕
senses.example: A fingerprint showed on the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃上显出一个指纹印。
senses.why: Finger plus print names the mark a finger prints onto a surface.
senses.whyCN: finger 加 print，直接命名手指印在表面上的那个痕迹。

senses.title: The ridge pattern used for identification
senses.definition: the pattern of ridges on a finger, used to prove who a person is
senses.definitionCN: 手指上的纹路图案，用于确认一个人的身份
senses.example: The police matched the fingerprint to the suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把指纹与嫌疑人对上了。
senses.why: Once the mark could be compared, the pattern itself became the identifying sense.
senses.whyCN: 一旦印痕可以比对，纹路本身就成了用于识别的义项。

senses.title: To record the fingerprints of a person
senses.definition: to take and record the fingerprints of someone
senses.definitionCN: 取下来并记录某人的指纹
senses.example: The officers fingerprinted everyone at the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 警员给现场的每个人都取了指纹。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb for the act of taking the mark.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，指取下这种印痕的动作。

senses.title: A unique digital trace
senses.definition: a set of data that identifies a device, a file, or a network connection
senses.definitionCN: 能识别一台设备、一个文件或一条网络连接的一组数据
senses.example: Every browser leaves a digital fingerprint.
senses.exampleCN: 每个浏览器都会留下数字指纹。
senses.why: Because a print proves identity, computing borrowed it for any unique trace.
senses.whyCN: 印痕能证明身份，计算机领域便借它指任何独特的痕迹。

senses.title: A chemical or genetic signature
senses.definition: a pattern of compounds or genes that identifies a substance or a living thing
senses.definitionCN: 能识别某种物质或生物的化合物或基因图案
senses.example: The lab produced a chemical fingerprint of the wine.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室给出了这款葡萄酒的化学特征谱。
senses.why: Science widened the identifying mark from skin to molecules and genes.
senses.whyCN: 科学把这种识别性印记从皮肤扩展到分子与基因。

intro.en: Fingerprint is a transparent English compound: finger names the digit, and print names the mark left by pressure.
intro.cn: fingerprint 是构词透明的英语复合词：finger 指手指，print 指受压留下的痕迹。

items.en: A reconstructed word such as fingraz is behind the English word for a finger.
items.cn: 重构形式 fingraz 是英语「手指」一词的前身。

items.en: Finger is the everyday Old English word for a digit of the hand.
items.cn: finger 是古英语中指手指的日常词。

items.en: Imprimere means to press into, and gives the idea of a mark pressed onto a surface.
items.cn: imprimere 意为压入，提供「压在表面上的痕迹」这一概念。

items.en: Empreinte means an impression stamped by pressure.
items.cn: empreinte 意为受压压出的印记。

items.en: Print names a mark made by pressing, and later a printed page.
items.cn: print 指压出的痕迹，后来又指印出的书页。

items.en: Fingerprint joins the two words as a term for identifying people.
items.cn: fingerprint 把两个词合成，用作识别身份的术语。

note.en: Fingerprint is built from finger and print, so it looks close to body-part words and to other print compounds.
note.cn: fingerprint 由 finger 与 print 构成，因此与身体部位词以及其它带 print 的复合词形近。

entries.definition: a digit of the hand
entries.definitionCN: 手指；构成 fingerprint 的前半部分

entries.definition: the end of a finger
entries.definitionCN: 指尖；与 fingerprint 同为 finger 构成的复合词

entries.definition: the mark left by a foot
entries.definitionCN: 脚印；与 fingerprint 共用 print 这一成分，但前半分别指手与足

entries.definition: the mark left by a thumb
a mark pressed into a surface
a small sign that something has been there

normalIntro.en: Fingerprint is a transparent compound: finger plus print, the mark a finger prints on a surface.
normalIntro.cn: fingerprint 是构词透明的复合词：finger 加 print，就是手指在表面印下的痕迹。

normal.en: Finger plus print makes fingerprint.
normal.cn: finger 加 print 就是 fingerprint。

normal.en: Police take a fingerprint to identify a person.
normal.cn: 警方取指纹以确认身份。

normal.en: A latent fingerprint is left on a surface and developed later.
normal.cn: latent fingerprint 指留在表面、事后再显影的指纹。

normal.en: Fingerprinting is the process of recording prints.
normal.cn: fingerprinting 是记录指纹的过程。

normal.en: A digital fingerprint identifies a device or a file.
normal.cn: digital fingerprint 用于识别设备或文件。

abstract.en: Press a fingertip on glass and see the oily ridges.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖按在玻璃上，留下油亮的螺纹。

abstract.en: Lay two ink cards side by side and match the whorls.
abstract.cn: 想象把两张墨印卡片并排比对螺纹。

abstract.en: Watch an officer roll a thumb across an ink pad.
abstract.cn: 想象警员把拇指在墨垫上滚过。

examples.en: The fingerprint on the glass matched the suspect.
examples.cn: 玻璃上的指纹与嫌疑人吻合。

examples.en: Every fingerprint is unique, even in identical twins.
examples.cn: 每个人的指纹都是独特的，同卵双胞胎也不例外。

examples.en: The app uses a fingerprint to unlock the phone.
examples.cn: 这个应用靠指纹解锁手机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「finger + print」——手指（finger）按出的印（print），字面就把答案说完了；这是拆词助记，与谐音无关，真正的词源见词根一栏。

root: 古英语 finger（手指）+ 中古英语 print（压出的印记，源自拉丁语 imprimere「压入」）→ 英语 fingerprint，核心义「手指压出的螺纹印记」。

sensesIntro.en: Fingerprint starts as the visible mark of a finger, becomes the ridge pattern used for identity, gains a verb sense, and then extends to digital and chemical signatures.
sensesIntro.cn: fingerprint 从手指留下的可见印痕开始，转为用于身份识别的纹路，再获得动词用法，最后扩展到数字与化学特征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whorl of ridges left on glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃上留下的一圈圈螺纹。

branches.en: The visible mark is the source sense.
branches.cn: 可见的印痕是最初的义项。

branches.en: A mark on a surface can be compared and so proves identity.
branches.cn: 表面上的印痕可以比对，因而能证明身份。

branches.en: If the pattern proves identity, taking it becomes an action.
branches.cn: 既然纹路能证明身份，取下它就成了一种动作。

branches.en: A unique trace in data does the same work as a print on glass.
branches.cn: 数据中的独特痕迹起着与玻璃上指纹相同的作用。

branches.en: Chemistry and genetics borrow the identifying pattern.
branches.cn: 化学与遗传学借用了这种识别性图案。

intro.en: Fingerprint is a native compound of finger and print; print itself came through French from Latin premere, to press.
intro.cn: fingerprint 是 finger 与 print 的英语复合词；print 经法语来自拉丁语 premere（压）。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere means to press, and imprimere means to press into, which yields the idea of a printed mark.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 premere 意为压，imprimere 意为压入，由此得到「印出的痕迹」这一概念。

items.example: Finger is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: finger 是这个复合词的前半。

items.example: Print is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: print 是这个复合词的后半。

items.example: The compound names the mark directly.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词直接命名了印痕。

items.example: The ending -s gives fingerprints.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 fingerprints。

items.example: Fingerprints adds the plural to the noun.
items.exampleCN: fingerprints 给名词加上复数。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms fingerprinting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 fingerprinting。

items.example: Fingerprinting names the whole procedure.
items.exampleCN: fingerprinting 指整套采集程序。

items.example: The prefix im- appears in imprimere.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 出现在 imprimere 中。

items.example: Imprint adds the idea of pressing in.
items.exampleCN: imprint 加上了「压入」的意思。

definition_zh: 有限的；有尽的；限定的
definition_en: having a limit or an end; not endless
core_image: 一条画到墙根就停住的线
scene: 预算有限，项目组只能砍掉一部分功能。With a finite budget, the team had to drop several features.
sceneCN: 这里 finite 是「有限的」（第 1 个义项：有数量或范围的限度）；句意：预算有限，团队不得不砍掉几项功能。

pos.zh: 有限之物（数学与哲学用语）

derivatives.zh: finite 加 -ly 构成，义为「有限地」
finite 加 -ness 构成，义为「有限性」
否定前缀 in- 加 finite 构成，义为「无限的」
由拉丁语 infinitas 借入，义为「无限；无穷」
由拉丁语 finitus 派生，义为「有限性；有尽」

senses.title: Having a limit or an end
senses.definition: having a boundary or an end, so that it does not go on forever
senses.definitionCN: 有边界或终点，不会永远延伸下去
senses.example: A line is finite, however far it is drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 无论画得多远，一条线总是有限的。
senses.why: The Latin root finis is a boundary, so anything with a boundary is finite.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 finis 意为边界，凡有边界之物便是「有限的」。

senses.title: Marked for tense and person in grammar
senses.definition: of a verb form, marked for tense and agreeing with its subject
senses.definitionCN: 动词形式带有时态标记并与主语保持一致
senses.example: A finite verb carries the tense of the clause.
senses.exampleCN: 限定动词承载整个小句的时态。
senses.why: A verb bounded by tense and person is limited in the way the word finis suggests.
senses.whyCN: 被时态与人称限定住的动词，正合 finis 所暗示的「受边界约束」。

senses.title: Countable in mathematics
senses.definition: of a set or number, having a definite countable size
senses.definitionCN: 集合或数量有确定的可数大小
senses.example: Every finite set has a largest element in this order.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种序下，每个有限集都有最大元。
senses.why: Mathematics keeps the plain idea of a boundary and makes it exact.
senses.whyCN: 数学保留了「有边界」的朴素意思，并把它精确化。

senses.title: Limited in supply
senses.definition: available only in a limited amount, so it can run out
senses.definitionCN: 只有有限的数量，因此可能用尽
senses.example: Oil is a finite resource.
senses.exampleCN: 石油是一种有限的资源。
senses.why: If a supply has a boundary, then it can be used up, which is the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 供应若有边界，就可能被用完，这就是最日常的义项。

senses.title: Bounded by death
senses.definition: of a life or a being, limited in time and therefore mortal
senses.definitionCN: 生命或存在者在时间上有限，因而会死
senses.example: Philosophers speak of finite beings who know they will end.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家谈论那些知道自己会终结的有限存在者。
senses.why: The same boundary that ends a line also ends a life, giving the word its solemn sense.
senses.whyCN: 给线段画上终点的那条边界也会给生命画上终点，于是有了庄重的义项。

intro.en: Finite comes from Latin finitus, the past participle of finire, to limit, and that verb rests on finis, a boundary.
intro.cn: finite 来自拉丁语 finitus，即 finire（限定）的过去分词，而 finire 又建立在 finis（边界）之上。

items.en: Finis means a boundary, an end, or the limit of a thing.
items.cn: finis 意为边界、终点或某物的限度。

items.en: Finire means to limit or to bring to an end.
items.cn: finire 意为限定或使结束。

items.en: Finitus, the past participle, means bounded or ended.
items.cn: 过去分词 finitus 意为被限定、被结束的。

items.en: Finit carries the sense of limited into French.
items.cn: finit 把「有限的」这一意思带入法语。

items.en: English borrows the word, spelled finit and then finite.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，先写作 finit，后定型为 finite。

items.en: Grammar and mathematics add their precise senses to the word.
items.cn: 语法学与数学为这个词添上各自的精确义项。

note.en: Finite looks close to infinite and definite, and it stands near the plain adjectives for limited things.
note.cn: finite 与 infinite、definite 形近，并与表示「受限」的普通形容词相邻。

entries.definition: having no limit or end
clear and fixed, with no doubt
the state of being limited
restricted in size or amount
entries.definitionCN: 在规模或数量上受限的

entries.definition: kept inside a border
able to be counted one by one

normalIntro.en: Finite carries Latin finis, the same boundary that ends a line or a life.
normalIntro.cn: finite 带着拉丁语 finis，就是给线段或生命画上终点的那条边界。

normal.en: Finite resources will run out one day.
normal.cn: 有限的资源终有一天会用尽。

normal.en: A finite verb carries tense and agrees with its subject.
normal.cn: 限定动词带时态并与主语一致。

normal.en: A finite set can be counted from first to last.
normal.cn: 有限集可以从头数到尾。

normal.en: The prefix in- turns finite into infinite.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 把 finite 变成 infinite。

normal.en: Finiteness is the state of having a limit.
normal.cn: finiteness 就是有边界的状态。

abstract.en: Draw a line that stops at a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一条线撞到墙就停住。

abstract.en: See a verb tied to its subject and its tense.
abstract.cn: 想象一个动词被主语和时态牢牢拴住。

abstract.en: Count a pile of stones until the pile is empty.
abstract.cn: 想象数一堆石子，直到堆里一颗不剩。

examples.en: The planet has finite resources.
examples.cn: 这颗行星的资源是有限的。

examples.en: A finite verb is marked for tense.
examples.cn: 限定动词带有时态标记。

examples.en: The algorithm works on any finite set of numbers.
examples.cn: 这个算法适用于任何有限的数集。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fin」是终点，加上形容词尾「-ite」，就成了「有终点的」，也就是有限；这是拆词助记，与谐音无关。

root: 拉丁语 finis（终点、边界）→ finire（限定、结束）→ finitus（被限定的）→ 英语 finite，核心义「有边界、有终点」。

sensesIntro.en: Finite begins with the plain idea of having a boundary, then serves grammar and mathematics, and ends with a limited supply or a bounded life.
sensesIntro.cn: finite 从「有边界」这一朴素意思开始，随后用于语法与数学，最后落到「供应有限」与「生命有尽」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that stops at a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条撞到墙便停下的线。

branches.en: Having a boundary is the source sense.
branches.cn: 有边界是最初的义项。

branches.en: A verb bounded by tense repeats the idea of a limit.
branches.cn: 被时态约束的动词重复了「限度」这一意思。

branches.en: A set with a boundary can be counted exactly.
branches.cn: 有边界的集合可以精确数清。

branches.en: A supply with a boundary can be used up.
branches.cn: 有边界的供应会被用完。

branches.en: A life with a boundary is mortal.
branches.cn: 有边界的生命终会结束。

intro.en: Finite is a Latin borrowing around finis, with English finitely, finiteness, and the negated infinite built on it.
intro.cn: finite 是围绕拉丁语 finis 的借词，英语在它之上构成 finitely、finiteness 以及加否定前缀的 infinite。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis means a boundary, finire means to limit, and finitus means limited.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 意为边界，finire 意为限定，finitus 意为被限定的。

items.example: Finis supplies the boundary image.
items.exampleCN: finis 提供「边界」这一意象。

items.example: Finire turns the noun into an action.
items.exampleCN: finire 把这个名词变成动作。

items.example: Finitus is the form English borrows.
items.exampleCN: finitus 是英语借入的形式。

items.meaningCN: 源自拉丁语 -itus 的形容词词尾
items.example: The ending -ite shapes finite.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ite 塑造了 finite 的形式。

items.example: Finite keeps the participle sense.
items.exampleCN: finite 保留了过去分词的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms finitely.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 finitely。

items.example: Finitely describes a limited action.
items.exampleCN: finitely 描述有限的动作。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms finiteness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 finiteness。

items.example: Finiteness names the state itself.
items.exampleCN: finiteness 直接命名这种状态。

items.example: The prefix in- forms infinite.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 infinite。

items.example: Infinite reverses the boundary sense.
items.exampleCN: infinite 反转了「边界」的含义。

definition_zh: 有限性；有限；限度；有穷性
definition_en: the quality or state of being finite, bounded, or limited
core_image: 一条路在两端各画着一道清楚的界线
scene: 深夜的病房里，老人第一次真切地感到生命的有限。On a quiet ward at midnight, the old man felt the finitude of his own life for the first time.
sceneCN: 这里「finitude」是「有限性」（第 1 个义项：事物有边界、有尽头的性质）；句意：深夜的病房里，老人第一次真切地感到自己生命的有限。

derivatives.zh: 有限的；有界的（同一拉丁词干 finitus 的形容词形式）
有限地；在有限范围内（finite 加 -ly 构成）
有限性（finite 加 -ness 构成，与 finitude 近义但更口语）

senses.title: The quality of having limits
senses.definition: the state of being limited in extent, size, or scope
senses.definitionCN: 在范围、大小或规模上受到限制的状态
senses.example: Every map has to reckon with the finitude of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 每一张地图都必须面对纸页篇幅的有限。
senses.why: Latin finis is a boundary line, so finitude names the condition of standing inside a drawn border.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 finis 是一条边界线，因此 finitude 指站在被画出的界线之内的状态。

senses.title: The limited span of a life
senses.definition: the condition of having a limited duration, especially of human existence
senses.definitionCN: 持续时间有限的状态，尤指人的存在
senses.example: Poets turn to finitude whenever they write about old age.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人写到老年时，总会转向生命的有限这一主题。
senses.why: Because a boundary is also an ending, the same noun came to name the shortness of a human life.
senses.whyCN: 因为边界同时也是终点，同一个名词便用来指人的一生之短。

senses.title: Finiteness in mathematics and philosophy
senses.definition: in mathematics and philosophy, the property of being finite rather than infinite
senses.definitionCN: 在数学与哲学中，指有限而非无限的性质
senses.example: The proof rests on the finitude of the set under study.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明依赖于所研究集合的有穷性。
senses.why: Technical fields took the plain sense of bounded extent and sharpened it into an exact property of sets and series.
senses.whyCN: 技术领域把「范围有界」的日常含义精确化为集合与数列的一种性质。

senses.title: One specific limit
senses.definition: a particular limit that restricts what something can do or become
senses.definitionCN: 限制某事物所能做到或所能成为的具体界限
senses.example: They named the finitude of the budget as the real obstacle.
senses.exampleCN: 他们指出预算的限度才是真正的障碍。
senses.why: The same noun can point at one concrete border instead of the general condition of being bordered.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可以指向某一条具体的界线，而不是「有界」这一总体状态。

intro.en: Finitude comes from Latin finis, a boundary or an end, by way of finire and the medieval noun finitudo.
intro.cn: finitude 源自拉丁语 finis（边界、终点），经 finire 与中世纪拉丁语 finitudo 进入法语和英语。

items.en: Finis names a boundary line, an end, or a limit.
items.cn: finis 指边界线、终点或限度。

items.en: Finire means to draw a boundary, to limit, or to bring to an end.
items.cn: finire 意为划定边界、加以限制或使某事先结束。

items.en: The participle finitus describes something bounded or finished.
items.cn: 分词 finitus 描述已完成或有边界的事物。

items.en: Finitudo, built on finitus, names the state of being bounded.
items.cn: 由 finitus 构成的中世纪拉丁语 finitudo 指「有界的状态」。

items.en: Finitude carries the abstract noun into French.
items.cn: finitude 把这个抽象名词带入法语。

items.en: English adopts the word in the seventeenth century and later adds mathematical and philosophical uses.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入这个词，后来又增添了数学与哲学用法。

note.en: Finitude belongs to the Latin family of boundaries and endings, and it sits close to words about limits and mortality.
note.cn: finitude 属于拉丁语中表示边界与终点的词族，与表示限度和必死的词相邻。

entries.definition: having bounds or limits
coming at the end, with nothing after it
to bring something to an end
a limit that restricts what something can do
the state of being subject to death
the quality of having limits

normalIntro.en: Finitude is the abstract noun of the boundary: finis drew the line, finitus marked what lies inside it.
normalIntro.cn: finitude 是「边界」的抽象名词：finis 画出界线，finitus 标出线内之物。

normal.en: The same stem gives finite, meaning limited, and infinite, meaning without limits.
normal.cn: 同一词干给出 finite（有限的）与 infinite（无限的）。

normal.en: Finitude is abstract, so it names a condition rather than one single border.
normal.cn: finitude 是抽象名词，因此它命名一种状态，而不是某一条界线。

normal.en: Finiteness is the plainer twin built with the suffix -ness.
normal.cn: finiteness 是用后缀 -ness 构成的更朴素的同义形式。

normal.en: Philosophers set finitude against infinity when they discuss human limits.
normal.cn: 哲学家讨论人的限度时，把 finitude 与 infinity 相对。

normal.en: A sense of finitude often appears in writing about old age and death.
normal.cn: 有限感常出现在关于老年与死亡的写作中。

abstract.en: Picture a road with a clear start and a clear end.
abstract.cn: 想象一条起点和终点都清清楚楚的路。

abstract.en: Think of one candle burning down inside a glass jar.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛在玻璃罐里一点点烧尽。

abstract.en: See a row of numbers that stops and goes no further.
abstract.cn: 想象一排数字到某处就停住，不再往后延伸。

examples.en: The novel keeps circling the finitude of memory.
examples.cn: 这部小说不断回到记忆的有限这一主题。

examples.en: Philosophers treat finitude as the mark of a created being.
examples.cn: 哲学家把有限性看作受造之物的标志。

examples.en: Any craft must accept the finitude of its materials.
examples.cn: 任何手艺都必须接受材料的限度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费尼图德」——读音近似「非你途的」，仿佛在说这条路不是你的，因为它总有尽头；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 finis（边界、终点）→ finire（划定界限、使结束）→ 分词 finitus（有界的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 finitudo（有界状态）→ 法语 finitude → 英语 finitude，核心义「被界线围住」。

sensesIntro.en: Finitude starts as the plain condition of having a boundary, extends to the short span of a human life, becomes an exact term in mathematics and philosophy, and can also name one concrete limit.
sensesIntro.cn: finitude 起初指「有边界」这一朴素状态，继而指人一生的短暂，在数学与哲学中成为精确术语，也可以指某一条具体的限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road with a drawn line at each end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条路在两端各画着一道界线。

branches.en: The plain state of having limits is the base sense of the word.
branches.cn: 「有界限」这一朴素状态是这个词的基础义项。

branches.en: A boundary is also an ending, which yields the sense of a limited life.
branches.cn: 边界同时也是终点，由此生出「生命有限」的义项。

branches.en: Mathematics and philosophy sharpen the base sense into an exact property.
branches.cn: 数学与哲学把基础义项精确化为一种性质。

branches.en: A general condition of being bounded can be narrowed to one specific limit.
branches.cn: 「有界」的总体状态可以收窄为某一条具体的限度。

branches.en: Both the span of a life and a finite set are measured against something endless.
branches.cn: 一生的长度与一个有限集合，都以某种无尽之物为参照。

intro.en: Finitude is built on the Latin boundary word finis, and English forms a small family around the same stem.
intro.cn: finitude 建在拉丁语表示边界的词 finis 上，英语围绕同一词干形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis means a boundary or an end, and finire means to bound or to finish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 意为边界或终点，finire 意为划界或结束。

items.example: Finis is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: finis 是整个词族的源头。

items.meaning: to bound, to limit, to finish
items.example: Finire turns the boundary into an action.
items.exampleCN: finire 把边界变成动作。

items.example: The participle supplies the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供形容词词干。

items.example: Finitudo is the abstract noun behind finitude.
items.exampleCN: finitudo 是 finitude 背后的抽象名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的后缀
items.example: The suffix -tude forms abstract nouns such as finitude.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tude 构成 finitude 这类抽象名词。

items.example: Finite is the everyday adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: finite 是词族中最日常的形容词。

items.example: The prefix in- negates the boundary.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定了边界。

items.example: Finiteness repeats the sense with a plainer suffix.
items.exampleCN: finiteness 用更朴素的后缀重复同一含义。

items.example: Define keeps the image of drawing a line around something.
items.exampleCN: define 保留着围出界线的意象。

items.example: Final marks the end point of the same root.
items.exampleCN: final 标出同一词根的终点。

definition_zh: 冷杉；枞树；冷杉木
definition_en: a tall evergreen conifer with needle-like leaves and upright cones, or the wood of this tree
core_image: 雪坡上一棵塔形常绿树，针叶暗绿而浓密
scene: 冬天的林子里，那棵针叶树还挂着青色的球果。In the winter woods, a tall fir still held its green cones.
sceneCN: 这里「fir」是「冷杉」（第 1 个义项：冷杉树）；句意：冬天的林子里，那棵冷杉还挂着青色的球果。

derivatives.zh: 冷杉的；多冷杉的（fir 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，较为少见）
冷杉木材（由 fir 与 wood 复合而成）
冷杉球果（fir 与 cone 构成的常用复合词）

senses.title: The evergreen conifer
senses.definition: a tall evergreen tree of the genus Abies, with needle-like leaves and upright cones
senses.definitionCN: 冷杉属的高大常绿乔木，具针状叶与直立球果
senses.example: A fir grows slowly but can live for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 冷杉长得慢，却能活上几百年。
senses.why: The Old English word named the resinous needle tree, and the tree itself is the first thing the word points at.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指的是多树脂的针叶树，树本身便是它最先指向的东西。

senses.title: The wood of this tree
senses.definition: the pale soft timber cut from such a tree, used in building and in paper making
senses.definitionCN: 由这种树取得的浅色软木材，用于建筑与造纸
senses.example: The shed was built of fir because the boards resist rot.
senses.exampleCN: 这间棚屋用冷杉木搭成，因为这种木板耐腐。
senses.why: Timber is named after the tree that produced it, so the material simply took over the same word.
senses.whyCN: 木材以其来源之树命名，于是这种材料直接沿用了同一个词。

senses.title: The loosely named conifers
senses.definition: a name loosely given to several conifers that are not true firs, such as the Douglas fir
senses.definitionCN: 被宽泛地用于几种并非真正冷杉的针叶树，如花旗松
senses.example: Walkers call the Douglas fir a true fir, though botanists place it in another genus.
senses.exampleCN: 徒步者把花旗松当作真正的冷杉，尽管植物学家把它归入另一属。
senses.why: True firs and their look-alikes share the same shape and habitat, so the common name spread beyond the genus.
senses.whyCN: 真正的冷杉与外形相似者共享同样的树形与生境，因此这个俗名越出了属的边界。

senses.title: A decorated winter tree
senses.definition: a fir cut and decorated as a Christmas tree
senses.definitionCN: 被砍下并装饰为圣诞树的冷杉
senses.example: They dragged a small fir into the hall and hung it with paper stars.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把一棵小冷杉拖进大厅，挂上纸星星。
senses.why: In northern Europe the fir became the festive evergreen, so the tree name stands for the decorated tree as well.
senses.whyCN: 在北欧，冷杉成为节日的常青树，于是树名也代指那棵装饰好的树。

intro.en: Fir goes back to Old English fyrh, from a reconstructed Germanic word for the resinous needle tree; a further link to the old Indo-European word for oak has been proposed but is not certain.
intro.cn: fir 源于古英语 fyrh，出自日耳曼语中表示多树脂针叶树的重构形式；一般认为它更早与印欧语表示「橡树」的词有关，但这一点并未确定。

items.en: Furho, a reconstructed form, names the resinous pine or fir.
items.cn: 重构形式 furho 指多树脂的松树或冷杉。

items.en: Fyrh and furh appear with the same meaning in Old English.
items.cn: 古英语中 fyrh 与 furh 表示同一意思。

items.en: The spelling settles into the shorter form fir.
items.cn: 拼写固定为较短的 fir。

items.en: Botanical writing fixes fir as the name of the true firs.
items.cn: 植物学写作把 fir 固定为真正冷杉的名称。

items.en: The timber trade and the Christmas custom widen the word.
items.cn: 木材贸易与圣诞习俗扩大了这个词的用法。

items.en: Douglas fir shows the name spreading to a different genus.
items.cn: 花旗松一名显示这个词已扩散到另一个属。

note.en: Fir is an old tree name that sounds like fur and fire, while its meaning neighbours are the other needle-bearing trees.
note.cn: fir 是古老的树名，读音接近 fur 与 fire；意义上的邻居是其他针叶树。

entries.definition: the soft hair covering an animal
entries.definitionCN: 动物的软毛；与 fir 只是拼写相近、读音相同，词源不同

entries.definition: burning flame
entries.definitionCN: 火；与 fir 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a narrow inlet of the sea
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄海湾；与 fir 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a conifer with needles growing in bundles
entries.definitionCN: 松树；针叶成束生长的针叶树

entries.definition: a conifer with drooping cones
entries.definitionCN: 云杉；球果下垂的针叶树

entries.definition: any tree that bears cones
entries.definitionCN: 针叶树；任何结球果的树

normalIntro.en: Fir is the short Old English name of the resinous needle tree, kept alive in compounds such as fir tree and Douglas fir.
normalIntro.cn: fir 是多树脂针叶树的古英语短名，在「fir tree」「Douglas fir」这类复合名称中沿用至今。

normal.en: Fir tree and fir cone are the two commonest compounds.
normal.cn: 「fir tree」与「fir cone」是最常见的两个复合词。

normal.en: Douglas fir is not a true fir, only a look-alike conifer.
normal.cn: 花旗松不是真正的冷杉，只是外形相似的针叶树。

normal.en: The word sounds exactly like fur, which causes spelling slips.
normal.cn: 这个词与「fur」读音相同，因此常出现拼写错误。

normal.en: Fir wood is pale, soft, and fairly resistant to rot.
normal.cn: 冷杉木颜色浅、材质软，而且比较耐腐。

normal.en: Silver fir and balsam fir are named for their needles and resin.
normal.cn: 银冷杉与香脂冷杉因针叶和树脂而得名。

abstract.en: See a dark green tower of branches standing in snow.
abstract.cn: 想象一座暗绿色的枝塔立在雪地里。

abstract.en: Run a hand along a pale, soft plank cut from the trunk.
abstract.cn: 想象用手抚过一块从树干上锯下的浅色软木板。

abstract.en: Notice a cone standing upright on a branch like a small barrel.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚球果像小木桶一样直立在枝头。

examples.en: The forest on the ridge is mostly fir and spruce.
examples.cn: 山脊上的森林主要是冷杉和云杉。

examples.en: A fir cone stood upright on the topmost branch.
examples.cn: 一枚冷杉球果直立在最高的枝条上。

examples.en: Builders prize fir for light framing that does not warp.
examples.cn: 建筑者看重冷杉木，因为它做轻质框架不易变形。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗」——读音像「毛皮」，可以想成披着一层厚毛的树，冷杉的针叶密得像一件毛大衣；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fyrh / furh（多树脂的针叶树）→ 中古英语 fir → 现代英语 fir；一般认为来自原始日耳曼语的重构形式 furho，更早的来源尚未确定。

sensesIntro.en: Fir names the tree first, then its timber, then spreads to look-alike conifers, and finally stands for the decorated winter tree.
sensesIntro.cn: fir 先指这种树，再指它的木材，随后扩展到外形相似的针叶树，最后代指装饰好的冬日之树。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark green tower of branches on a snowy slope.
core.cn: 核心意象：雪坡上一座暗绿色的枝塔。

branches.en: The tree itself is the base sense of the word.
branches.cn: 树本身是这个词的基础义项。

branches.en: Timber takes over the name of the tree that produced it.
branches.cn: 木材沿用了产出它的那棵树的名字。

branches.en: The common name spreads to conifers of other genera.
branches.cn: 这个俗名扩散到其他属的针叶树。

branches.en: The festive use narrows the word to one decorated tree.
branches.cn: 节日用法把词义收窄到那一棵装饰好的树。

branches.en: True firs and the Douglas fir share needles, resin, and a conical habit.
branches.cn: 真正的冷杉与花旗松共享针叶、树脂与锥形树姿。

intro.en: Fir is a native Germanic tree name, so its word family is small and consists mostly of compounds.
intro.cn: fir 是本土的日耳曼语树名，因此词族很小，主要由复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Fir has no Latin source; the botanical genus name Abies was taken from Greek and latinized later, so no Latin cognate is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: fir 没有拉丁语来源；植物学属名 Abies 取自希腊语，后来才拉丁化，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Fyrh is the earliest recorded form of the word.
items.exampleCN: fyrh 是这个词最早记录的形式。

items.example: Furho is a reconstructed form, marked with an asterisk in handbooks.
items.exampleCN: furho 是重构形式，在手册中带星号标注。

items.example: Fir keeps both the tree sense and the timber sense.
items.exampleCN: fir 同时保留树与木材两个义项。

items.example: Firs and spruces fill the higher slopes.
items.exampleCN: 冷杉与云杉长满较高的山坡。

items.example: Firry is a rare adjective for a wooded slope.
items.exampleCN: firry 是形容多冷杉山坡的少见形容词。

items.example: Firwood names the timber rather than the standing tree.
items.exampleCN: firwood 指木材，而不是立着的树。

items.example: Fir tree is the everyday spoken name.
items.exampleCN: fir tree 是日常口语中的叫法。

items.example: Fir cone points upward on the branch.
items.exampleCN: 冷杉球果在枝头朝上立着。

items.meaning: a western conifer of another genus
items.example: Douglas fir is a look-alike rather than a true fir.
items.exampleCN: 花旗松是外形相似者，而非真正的冷杉。

items.meaning: the genus of the true firs
items.example: Abies is the botanical label for the true firs.
items.exampleCN: Abies 是真正冷杉的植物学属名。

definition_zh: 灭火；消防工作；消防的
definition_en: the work of putting out fires, especially as an organized occupation or public service
core_image: 水柱压住门里窜出的火舌，白烟腾起
scene: 半夜警铃响起，值班的队员摸黑穿好装备。Within a minute of the alarm, the crew was dressed and ready for firefighting.
sceneCN: 这里「firefighting」是「灭火、消防工作」（第 1 个义项：把火扑灭的行动）；句意：警铃响后一分钟内，队员就穿好装备准备投入灭火。

pos.zh: 消防的；灭火用的（用于名词前）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多次灭火行动）

derivatives.zh: 消防员（由 firefighting 去掉 -ing 再加 -er 构成的施事名词）
交火；（口语）灭火战斗（fire 与 fight 复合，与 firefighting 同源）
消防站（fire 与 house 复合，属同一词族的场所名称）

senses.title: The act of putting out a fire
senses.definition: the work of extinguishing a fire that is already burning
senses.definitionCN: 把已经烧起来的火扑灭的工作
senses.example: Firefighting began the moment the roof caught.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶一着火，灭火工作就开始了。
senses.why: Fire names the flame and fighting names the struggle, so the compound literally describes a fight against fire.
senses.whyCN: fire 指火焰，fighting 指搏斗，因此这个复合词字面上就是「与火搏斗」。

senses.title: The occupation and public service
senses.definition: the organized profession and public service that deals with fires
senses.definitionCN: 以应对火灾为职责的有组织职业与公共服务
senses.example: She joined firefighting because her father had served in the same brigade.
senses.exampleCN: 她加入消防这一行，因为她父亲也曾在同一支队伍里服役。
senses.why: Once cities hired full-time crews, the activity became an institution, and the word took on the trade itself.
senses.whyCN: 当城市开始雇用专职队伍，这项活动变成一种制度，这个词也就指这门职业。

senses.title: Reactive crisis management
senses.titleCN: 救火式的应急处理（比喻）
senses.definition: the constant handling of urgent problems instead of long-term planning
senses.definitionCN: 只顾应付紧急问题而缺少长期规划的状态
senses.example: The department spends its days in firefighting rather than in design.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部门整天忙于救火，而不是做设计。
senses.why: A crew that only reacts to alarms never plans, so rushing to fires became an image for reactive management.
senses.whyCN: 只会闻警而动的队伍从不做规划，于是「赶去救火」的意象被用来指被动应付的管理方式。

senses.title: The attributive use
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe equipment, teams, or measures for fighting fires
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，描述用于灭火的设备、队伍或措施
senses.example: The grant bought firefighting gear for three rural stations.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔拨款为三个乡村消防站购置了灭火装备。
senses.why: English lets a gerund stand as a modifier, so the name of the activity also labels whatever serves it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让动名词直接充当修饰语，于是这项活动的名称也用来标注为其服务的事物。

intro.en: Firefighting is a transparent English compound of fire and fighting, recorded from the nineteenth century as paid fire brigades spread through industrial cities.
intro.cn: firefighting 是 fire 与 fighting 构成的透明复合词，一般认为随有偿消防队在工业城市普及而于十九世纪见于记载。

items.en: Fyr names fire, the flame that the word will fight.
items.cn: fyr 指火，也就是这个词要去搏斗的火焰。

items.en: Feohtan means to fight, from a Germanic verb of combat.
items.cn: feohtan 意为搏斗，来自日耳曼语的战斗动词。

items.en: Fighting, the gerund of fight, names the struggle itself.
items.cn: fighting 是 fight 的动名词，指搏斗本身。

items.en: Firefighting appears as paid brigades replace volunteer bucket lines.
items.cn: 当有偿消防队取代义务提水队，firefighting 一词开始出现。

items.en: The word widens to aerial firefighting and wildland firefighting.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到空中灭火与野外火灾扑救。

items.en: Management writing borrows it for reactive crisis work.
items.cn: 管理学写作借它指被动应付的危机处理。

note.en: Firefighting is the fire branch of the fight family, and its meaning neighbours are the services, tools, and habits that surround a blaze.
note.cn: firefighting 是 fight 词族中的「火」这一支，意义上的邻居是围绕火灾的队伍、工具与做法。

entries.definition: a person whose job is to put out fires
an exchange of gunfire, or a battle against a fire
an older word for a person who fights fires
an organized unit that puts out fires
the technical term for putting out a fire
entries.definitionCN: 火灾扑救；灭火（技术用语）

entries.definition: handling an emergency as it happens

normalIntro.en: Firefighting joins two plain Old English words, fire and fighting, so the compound needs no explanation.
normalIntro.cn: firefighting 由两个朴素的古英语词 fire 与 fighting 拼合，整个复合词几乎不需要解释。

normal.en: The -ing ending makes it a name for the activity rather than for the person.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ing 让它成为这项活动的名称，而不是人的名称。

normal.en: Add -er and you get firefighter, the person who does the work.
normal.cn: 加上 -er 就得到 firefighter，指从事这项工作的人。

normal.en: Firefighting gear, firefighting foam, and firefighting team are ordinary collocations.
normal.cn: 「firefighting gear」「firefighting foam」「firefighting team」都是常见搭配。

normal.en: Aerial firefighting uses aircraft instead of hose lines.
normal.cn: 空中灭火用飞机代替水带。

normal.en: In business writing, firefighting means reacting to problems all day.
normal.cn: 在商业写作中，firefighting 指整天被动应付问题。

abstract.en: Hear the hiss of water striking hot metal.
abstract.cn: 想象水柱打在灼热金属上发出的嘶声。

abstract.en: See a line of helmets passing buckets hand to hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一队头盔下的人把水桶一个个传过去。

abstract.en: Picture a desk buried in urgent notes, none of them planned.
abstract.cn: 想象一张堆满紧急便条的桌子，没有一件是计划内的。

examples.en: Firefighting in the hills lasted three days and nights.
examples.cn: 山区的灭火行动持续了三天三夜。

examples.en: The town doubled its firefighting budget after the warehouse blaze.
examples.cn: 仓库大火之后，小镇把消防预算翻了一倍。

examples.en: Good managers plan ahead instead of constant firefighting.
examples.cn: 好的管理者会提前规划，而不是不断救火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「发一儿发一听」——读快了像「fire fight in」，仿佛在说在火里打一场架；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fyr（火）+ feohtan（搏斗）→ 中古英语 fight 及其动名词 fighting → 十九世纪复合为 firefighting，字面义「与火搏斗」，核心义「把火扑灭」。

sensesIntro.en: Firefighting names the act first, then the trade, then the reactive style of work, and finally the attributive label for gear and teams.
sensesIntro.cn: firefighting 先指灭火这一动作，再指这门职业，随后指被动应付的工作方式，最后作定语标注装备与队伍。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stream of water driving back a tongue of flame.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股水柱把火舌压回去。

branches.en: The act of extinguishing a blaze is the base sense.
branches.cn: 把火扑灭这一动作是基础义项。

branches.en: Repeated acts become an institution, which yields the occupational sense.
branches.cn: 反复的行动变成制度，由此生出职业义项。

branches.en: The image of rushing to alarms extends to reactive management.
branches.cn: 「闻警即动」的意象延伸到被动应付的管理方式。

branches.en: A gerund can modify a noun, so the activity names the gear it uses.
branches.cn: 动名词可以修饰名词，于是这项活动也用来命名它所用的装备。

branches.en: The act and the profession share one word because the trade grew out of the act.
branches.cn: 动作与职业共用一个词，因为这门行业正是从这一动作生长出来的。

intro.en: Firefighting is a native compound, built from fire, fight, and the gerund suffix -ing, with firefighter as its best known derivative.
intro.cn: firefighting 是本土复合词，由 fire、fight 与动名词后缀 -ing 构成，最知名的派生词是 firefighter。

latinIntro.en: Both fire and fight are Germanic, with no Latin cognates; Latin ignis and pugnare are only translation equivalents.
latinIntro.cn: fire 与 fight 都属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同源词；拉丁语 ignis 与 pugnare 只是含义对应的译词。

items.example: Fyr is the Old English ancestor of fire.
items.exampleCN: fyr 是 fire 的古英语前身。

items.example: Feohtan supplies the fighting half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: feohtan 提供这个复合词中「搏斗」的一半。

items.example: Fight keeps both the physical and the figurative struggle.
items.exampleCN: fight 同时保留身体与比喻两种搏斗。

items.meaningCN: 构成动名词与活动名词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing turns fight into the name of an activity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 把 fight 变成活动名称。

items.meaning: a person who puts out fires
items.example: Firefighter adds the agent suffix -er.
items.exampleCN: firefighter 加上施事后缀 -er。

items.meaning: an exchange of gunfire, or a battle against fire
items.example: Firefight is the shorter compound behind the longer word.
items.exampleCN: firefight 是较长那个词背后的短复合词。

items.example: A fire engine carries the pumps and hoses.
items.exampleCN: 消防车装载水泵与水带。

items.example: The fire brigade is the unit, firefighting is the work.
items.exampleCN: fire brigade 指队伍，firefighting 指工作。

items.meaning: foam used to smother fuel fires
items.example: Firefighting foam smothers a fuel fire rather than cooling it.
items.exampleCN: 灭火泡沫靠窒息而非降温来对付油火。

items.example: Wildland firefighting depends on wind and terrain.
items.exampleCN: 野外火灾扑救取决于风向与地形。

definition_zh: 萤火虫；萤光；发光的甲虫
definition_en: a small beetle that glows in the dark, or the cold light it produces
core_image: 夏夜草丛里一点黄绿色的光忽明忽暗
scene: 夏夜的稻田边，一点微光在草叶间升起又落下。By the rice field on a summer night, a single firefly rose and fell among the blades of grass.
sceneCN: 这里「firefly」是「萤火虫」（第 1 个义项：会发光的甲虫）；句意：夏夜的稻田边，一只萤火虫在草叶间升起又落下。

forms.label: 相关形容词（萤火虫似的）
复合术语（萤火虫荧光素酶）

derivatives.zh: 萤火虫似的（firefly 加后缀 -like 构成，形容忽明忽暗的光）
萤火虫荧光素酶（取自萤火虫发光器官的酶，为生物化学术语）

senses.title: The glowing beetle
senses.definition: a soft-bodied beetle of the family Lampyridae, whose abdomen produces light
senses.definitionCN: 萤科中腹部能发光的软体甲虫
senses.example: A firefly blinked twice above the wet grass.
senses.exampleCN: 一只萤火虫在湿草上方闪了两下。
senses.why: Fire names the glow and fly names the winged insect, so the compound points straight at a flying spark.
senses.whyCN: fire 指火光，fly 指有翅的昆虫，因此这个复合词直接指向「会飞的火星」。

senses.title: The cold light itself
senses.definition: the pale yellow-green light produced by the beetle, used mainly to attract a mate
senses.definitionCN: 这种甲虫发出的淡黄绿色冷光，主要用于吸引配偶
senses.example: The firefly glow lasted a second, then the meadow went dark.
senses.exampleCN: 那点萤光只亮了一秒，随后草地便暗了下来。
senses.why: Because the glow is the most conspicuous part of the insect, its name can stand for the light alone.
senses.whyCN: 因为光是这种昆虫最显眼的部分，虫名可以单独指那点光。

senses.title: A brief brightness in the dark
senses.definition: a person or thing that shines briefly and then disappears
senses.definitionCN: 短暂发光随后消失的人或事物
senses.example: Her idea was a firefly in a long, dull meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她的想法是漫长沉闷会议里的一点萤光。
senses.why: The insect appears for a few summer weeks and vanishes, so the image serves for anything brief and bright.
senses.whyCN: 这种昆虫只在夏季出现几周便消失，因此这个意象可指任何短暂而明亮的事物。

senses.title: A loose name for other glowing insects
senses.definition: a popular name also given to glow-worms and similar luminous insects
senses.definitionCN: 也通俗地用于萤火虫以外的发光昆虫，如无翅的雌性萤类
senses.example: In Britain, children still call the wingless glow-worm a firefly.
senses.exampleCN: 在英国，孩子们仍把无翅的「glow-worm」叫作「firefly」。
senses.why: Popular naming groups any small light in the grass under one familiar word.
senses.whyCN: 民间命名把草丛里的小光点都归到同一个熟悉的词下。

intro.en: Firefly is a plain English compound of fire and fly, first recorded in the seventeenth century and especially common in American usage.
intro.cn: firefly 是 fire 与 fly 构成的朴素英语复合词，一般认为首见于十七世纪，在美式英语中尤为常见。

items.en: Fyr names fire, the glow that the insect carries.
items.cn: fyr 指火，也就是这种昆虫携带的光。

items.en: Fleoge means a fly, from a verb meaning to fly.
items.cn: fleoge 指苍蝇一类的小虫，出自意为「飞」的动词。

items.en: The insect word settles into the shorter form flye.
items.cn: 指虫的词固定为较短的 flye。

items.en: The compound firefly is recorded, naming a winged insect that glows.
items.cn: 复合词 firefly 见于记载，指会发光的飞虫。

items.en: American usage prefers firefly, while British English often says glow-worm.
items.cn: 美式英语多用 firefly，英式英语则常说 glow-worm。

items.en: Laboratory science borrows firefly luciferase for the light-producing enzyme.
items.cn: 实验室科学借 firefly luciferase 指那种产生光的酶。

note.en: Firefly is built from two everyday words, fire and fly, and its meaning neighbours are the other insects that light up a summer night.
note.cn: firefly 由 fire 与 fly 两个日常词构成，意义上的邻居是其他会在夏夜发光的昆虫。

entries.definition: flame and heat
entries.definitionCN: 火；构成 firefly 的前半部分

entries.definition: a small winged insect
entries.definitionCN: 飞虫；构成 firefly 的后半部分

entries.definition: a device that explodes with light and colour
entries.definitionCN: 烟花；与 firefly 共享 fire 这一成分

entries.definition: a wingless beetle whose female glows in the dark
entries.definitionCN: 萤火虫的一类；雌性无翅而在暗处发光

entries.definition: the American name for a firefly
an insect with hard wing cases
entries.definitionCN: 甲虫；有坚硬鞘翅的昆虫

normalIntro.en: Firefly is a two-word picture: fire plus fly, a flying spark in the dark.
normalIntro.cn: firefly 是一幅两词拼成的画：火加飞虫，就是黑夜里飞着的火星。

normal.en: The plural fireflies changes the y to ies, as with butterfly.
normal.cn: 复数 fireflies 把词尾 y 变成 ies，与 butterfly 的变化相同。

normal.en: Firefly light and firefly glow both name the cold light of the beetle.
normal.cn: 「firefly light」与「firefly glow」都指这种甲虫的冷光。

normal.en: American speakers say firefly, British speakers often say glow-worm.
normal.cn: 美国人说 firefly，英国人常说 glow-worm。

normal.en: Firefly luciferase is the enzyme that makes the light in the laboratory.
normal.cn: firefly luciferase 是实验室里用来产生光的那种酶。

normal.en: The compound is transparent, so fire and fly keep their plain meanings.
normal.cn: 这个复合词很透明，fire 与 fly 都保持各自的本义。

abstract.en: Watch one green point switch on, then off, above wet grass.
abstract.cn: 想象湿草上方一个绿色小点亮了又灭。

abstract.en: Hold a cool light in your palm that gives no heat.
abstract.cn: 想象掌心托着一点不发热的冷光。

abstract.en: See a bright idea flare up in a dark room and fade.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里一个明亮的念头闪起又暗下去。

examples.en: Fireflies filled the hedge on the first warm evening.
examples.cn: 第一个暖和的傍晚，树篱里满是萤火虫。

examples.en: The firefly flashed once and the grass answered with three more.
examples.cn: 那只萤火虫闪了一下，草丛里又回应了三下。

examples.en: Pesticides have thinned the firefly population near the orchard.
examples.cn: 农药让果园附近的萤火虫种群变少了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「发一弗莱」——像「fire 飞了」，一团火飞起来，就成了夜里提灯的小虫；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fyr（火）+ fleoge（飞虫）→ 十七世纪复合为 firefly，字面义「带着火的飞虫」，核心义「黑夜里发光的小甲虫」。

sensesIntro.en: Firefly names the insect first, then its cold light, then any brief bright thing, and finally the loose popular label for other glowing insects.
sensesIntro.cn: firefly 先指这种昆虫，再指它的冷光，随后指任何短暂明亮的事物，最后成为其他发光昆虫的通俗称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one green point of light above wet grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿草上方的一点绿光。

branches.en: The glowing beetle is the base sense of the word.
branches.cn: 会发光的甲虫是这个词的基础义项。

branches.en: The light is the most visible part, so the name can stand for it alone.
branches.cn: 光是最显眼的部分，因此虫名可以单独指那点光。

branches.en: A short summer appearance turns the insect into an image of brief brightness.
branches.cn: 短暂的夏季现身使这种昆虫成为「明亮而短暂」的意象。

branches.en: Popular naming extends the word to other luminous insects.
branches.cn: 民间命名把这个词扩展到其他发光昆虫。

branches.en: Insect and light share one name because the glow is how the beetle is found.
branches.cn: 虫与光共用一个名字，因为人正是靠那点光发现这种甲虫的。

intro.en: Firefly is a native compound of two Old English words, with firefly-like and firefly luciferase as its modern extensions.
intro.cn: firefly 是由两个古英语词构成的本土复合词，现代扩展形式有 firefly-like 与 firefly luciferase。

latinIntro.en: Fire and fly are Germanic, with no Latin cognates; the family name Lampyridae comes from Greek lampas, a torch, and is not a source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: fire 与 fly 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同源词；科名 Lampyridae 来自希腊语 lampas（火炬），并不是这个英语词的来源。

items.example: Fyr is the fire half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: fyr 是这个复合词中「火」的一半。

items.example: Fleoge is the fly half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: fleoge 是这个复合词中「飞虫」的一半。

items.example: Fly keeps the insect sense in the modern compound.
items.exampleCN: fly 在近代复合词中保留昆虫义。

items.example: Firefly joins the two halves into one insect name.
items.exampleCN: firefly 把两半合成一个虫名。

items.example: Fireflies changes y to ies in the plural.
items.exampleCN: fireflies 复数把 y 变成 ies。

items.example: The suffix -like forms firefly-like.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -like 构成 firefly-like。

items.meaning: resembling a firefly or its light
items.example: Firefly-like describes a flickering glow.
items.exampleCN: firefly-like 形容忽明忽暗的光。

items.example: Luciferase names the enzyme, from Latin lux, light.
items.exampleCN: luciferase 指这种酶，词源是拉丁语 lux（光）。

items.meaning: the light-making enzyme of the firefly
items.example: Firefly luciferase is used as a marker in laboratories.
items.exampleCN: 萤火虫荧光素酶在实验室里用作标记。

items.example: Lampyridae is the zoological family name, from Greek.
items.exampleCN: Lampyridae 是动物学上的科名，来自希腊语。

definition_zh: 渔业；渔场；养鱼场
definition_en: the business of catching fish, or a place where fish are caught or raised
core_image: 清晨的海湾里，几艘小船围着一片插满浮标的水域下网
scene: 清晨的海湾里，几艘小船驶向同一片插着浮标的水域下网。The boats sailed out to the same fishery at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 fishery 是「渔场」（第 2 个义项：捕鱼的水域）；句意：清晨，小船驶向同一片渔场。

derivatives.zh: 在 fish 后加 -er 构成，指以捕鱼为业的人，即渔民
fish 加 -ing 构成，指捕鱼这一活动，偏重动作本身
由 fisher 与 man 复合而成，指捕鱼的男子，即渔夫

senses.title: The fishing industry
senses.definition: the business or occupation of catching fish and other sea animals
senses.definitionCN: 捕捞鱼类及其他海洋动物的行业或职业
senses.example: The island depends on its fishery for most of its income.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的大部分收入依赖其渔业。
senses.why: The suffix -ery turns the act of fishing into a trade or industry.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ery 把「捕鱼」这一动作变成一种行业，所以 fishery 可以指渔业。

senses.title: A fishing ground
senses.definition: an area of water where fish are caught, especially one used regularly
senses.definitionCN: 捕捞鱼类的水域，尤指经常使用的捕鱼区
senses.example: The fleet returned to its usual fishery near the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 船队回到了礁石附近常去的渔场。
senses.why: A place where the trade is carried on naturally takes the name of the trade itself.
senses.whyCN: 从事这一行业的地方自然沿用了行业本身的名称，于是 fishery 也指渔场。

senses.title: A fish farm
senses.definition: a place where fish are bred and raised for food
senses.definitionCN: 繁殖和养殖食用鱼的地方
senses.example: The new fishery raises salmon in floating cages.
senses.exampleCN: 新养鱼场在浮动网箱里养殖鲑鱼。
senses.why: Raising fish repeats the same place-and-activity pattern, so the word covers farms as well.
senses.whyCN: 养鱼延续了「场所加活动」的同一构词思路，因此这个词也覆盖养鱼场。

senses.title: A fishing enterprise
senses.definition: a company or establishment that catches or processes fish
senses.definitionCN: 捕捞或加工鱼类的公司或机构
senses.example: The family runs a small fishery on the northern coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人在北岸经营一家小型渔业企业。
senses.why: An organised business is the industry sense made concrete.
senses.whyCN: 有组织的企业是「行业」义项的具体化，所以 fishery 也可指渔业企业。

senses.title: The right to fish
senses.definition: the legal right to catch fish in particular waters
senses.definitionCN: 在特定水域捕捞鱼类的法定权利
senses.example: The court confirmed the ancient fishery of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 法院确认了该村由来已久的捕鱼权。
senses.why: A right attached to a place of fishing extends the place sense into law.
senses.whyCN: 附着于捕鱼地点的权利，把「渔场」义项延伸到法律领域。

senses.title: The fish stock
senses.definition: the population of fish in a particular area, treated as a resource
senses.definitionCN: 某一区域被视为资源的鱼类种群
senses.example: Scientists warn that the fishery may collapse within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家警告，该鱼类资源可能在十年内崩溃。
senses.why: Modern management treats the fish themselves as the resource behind the industry.
senses.whyCN: 现代管理把鱼本身视为行业背后的资源，于是 fishery 也指鱼类资源。

intro.en: Fishery is generally explained as the Old English word for fish plus the Romance suffix -ery, perhaps modelled on Old French pescherie.
intro.cn: 一般认为，fishery 是古英语表示「鱼」的词加上罗曼语后缀 -ery 构成的，可能受到古法语 pescherie 的影响。

items.en: Fisc means fish and supplies the base of the word.
items.cn: fisc 意为鱼，提供这个词的词基。

items.en: -aria is the Latin suffix behind -ery, naming a place or an activity.
items.cn: -aria 是 -ery 背后的拉丁语后缀，表示地点或活动。

items.en: -erie carries the suffix into French, and pescherie may have shaped the English form.
items.cn: -erie 把这一后缀带入法语，而 pescherie 可能影响了英语形式。

items.en: Fischerie names both the fishing trade and the ground where it is carried on.
items.cn: 中古英语 fischerie 既指捕鱼行业，也指从事捕鱼的水域。

items.en: Fishery extends to fish farms, fishing rights and managed fish stocks.
items.cn: 现代英语中，fishery 扩展到养鱼场、捕鱼权与受管理的鱼类资源。

note.en: Fishery belongs to the fish family and to the language of catching, farming and regulating fish.
note.cn: fishery 属于「鱼」词族，也属于捕鱼、养殖与管理的用语。

entries.definition: a person who catches fish
the activity of catching fish
an animal that lives in water and has fins
entries.definitionCN: 鱼；生活在水中的有鳍动物

entries.definition: fishing with a rod and line
the farming of fish and water plants
a place where eggs are hatched and young fish are raised
entries.definitionCN: 孵化鱼卵并养育幼鱼的场所

normalIntro.en: Fishery is fish plus -ery: the fish, the place, and the trade share one word.
normalIntro.cn: fishery 就是 fish 加 -ery：鱼、场所与行业共用一个词。

normal.en: Fish is the base, and -ery adds the idea of a place or a trade.
normal.cn: fish 是词基，-ery 加上「场所」或「行业」的含义。

normal.en: A fishery can be a ground, a farm, or an industry.
normal.cn: fishery 可以是渔场、养鱼场，也可以是渔业。

normal.en: Coastal fishery and inland fishery name two kinds of fishing ground.
normal.cn: 「coastal fishery」与「inland fishery」指两类渔场。

normal.en: Fishery management keeps the fish stock healthy.
normal.cn: 「fishery management」让鱼类资源保持健康。

normal.en: Compare fishing, the activity, with fishery, the place or business.
normal.cn: 对比表示活动的 fishing 与表示场所或行业的 fishery。

abstract.en: Picture a net hauled onto a deck, the catch turned into a livelihood.
abstract.cn: 想象渔网被拖上甲板，渔获变成生计。

abstract.en: See a line of buoys marking one stretch of water.
abstract.cn: 想象一排浮标围出一片水域。

abstract.en: See floating cages holding farmed salmon.
abstract.cn: 想象浮动网箱里养着鲑鱼。

examples.en: The small fishery employs half the village.
examples.cn: 这家小型渔业企业雇用了半个村子的人。

examples.en: The fishery in the bay is closed during the spawning season.
examples.cn: 海湾渔场在产卵季节关闭。

examples.en: Overfishing has pushed the fishery to the edge of collapse.
examples.cn: 过度捕捞已把这片鱼类资源推到崩溃边缘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费雪莉」——想象一位叫费雪莉的渔家姑娘站在码头清点渔获；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fisc（鱼）+ 源自古法语的 -ery（表示场所或行业）→ 中古英语 fischerie → 英语 fishery，核心义「与捕鱼相关的地方或行业」。

sensesIntro.en: Fishery starts as the trade of catching fish, then names the water, the farm, the firm, the right, and finally the fish stock itself.
sensesIntro.cn: fishery 从捕鱼行业开始，继而指水域、养鱼场、企业、权利，最后指鱼类资源本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a net drawn around one stretch of water.
core.cn: 核心意象：渔网围出一片水域。

branches.en: The trade of catching fish is the base sense.
branches.cn: 捕鱼行业是基础义项。

branches.en: A ground and a fishing right both tie the trade to particular water.
branches.cn: 渔场与捕鱼权都把行业绑定在特定水域。

branches.en: Fish farming repeats the place pattern for raised fish.
branches.cn: 养鱼场把「场所」模式用在养殖鱼上。

branches.en: An enterprise is the industry made concrete.
branches.cn: 企业是行业的具体形态。

branches.en: The stock sense treats the fish as a managed resource.
branches.cn: 鱼类资源义把鱼视为受管理的资源。

intro.en: Fishery joins a Germanic word for fish to a Romance suffix, so the word carries both a native noun and a borrowed ending.
intro.cn: fishery 把日耳曼语中表示「鱼」的词与罗曼语后缀结合起来，因此既有本族词基，也有借来的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies only the suffix -aria, the source of -ery; Latin piscis is not related to fish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只提供了后缀 -aria，即 -ery 的来源；拉丁语 piscis 与 fish 并没有同源关系。

items.example: Fisc is the old Germanic name for fish.
items.exampleCN: fisc 是鱼在日耳曼语中的古称。

items.meaning: a water animal, or to catch fish
items.example: Fish is the modern form of fisc.
items.exampleCN: fish 是 fisc 的现代形式。

items.example: The suffix -ery makes fishery a place or a business.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ery 使 fishery 表示场所或行业。

items.meaning: the fishing trade or a fishing ground
items.example: Fishery keeps both the place and the trade senses.
items.exampleCN: fishery 同时保留场所与行业两种含义。

items.example: Fisher adds -er to the base fish.
items.exampleCN: fisher 在词基 fish 后加 -er。

items.example: Fishing names the activity, not the place.
items.exampleCN: fishing 指活动，不指场所。

items.example: Fisherman joins fisher and man.
items.exampleCN: fisherman 由 fisher 与 man 组合而成。

items.example: -erie is the French form behind -ery.
items.exampleCN: -erie 是 -ery 背后的法语形式。

items.meaningCN: 渔业、渔场或鱼类资源的复数形式
items.example: Fisheries is the plural of fishery.
items.exampleCN: fisheries 是 fishery 的复数。

latinEntries.meaning: a place or an activity connected with a thing
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与某事物有关的地点或活动

definition_zh: 裂变；分裂；细胞分裂
definition_en: the splitting of an atomic nucleus or a living cell, or any act of dividing into parts
core_image: 一颗沉重的大球被中子击中，裂成两半并放出能量
scene: 实验记录里，一颗重原子核被中子击中后分成两块，同时释放出大量能量。A neutron struck the heavy nucleus, and fission released a burst of energy.
sceneCN: 这里 fission 是「核裂变」（第 2 个义项：原子核分裂并释放能量）；句意：中子击中重原子核，裂变释放出一股能量。

derivatives.zh: fission 加 -able 构成，指能够发生裂变的
与 fission 同源，指容易裂变的，尤指可被中子分裂的
与 fission 共享「劈开」词根，指岩石或组织上的裂缝

senses.title: Nuclear fission
senses.definition: the splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus into lighter nuclei, with a release of energy
senses.definitionCN: 重原子核分裂成较轻原子核并释放能量的过程
senses.example: A single neutron can start fission in a uranium nucleus.
senses.exampleCN: 一个中子就能让铀原子核开始裂变。
senses.why: The Latin root means to split, and physics applies it to the nucleus that splits.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「劈开」，物理学把它用在会分裂的原子核上。

senses.title: Cell division
senses.definition: a form of reproduction in which a cell divides into two or more new cells
senses.definitionCN: 细胞分成两个或多个新细胞的一种繁殖方式
senses.example: Bacteria reproduce by fission, doubling their numbers quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌通过分裂繁殖，数量很快翻倍。
senses.why: Living cells split in the same way, so biology borrowed the word for its dividing cells.
senses.whyCN: 活细胞也以同样的方式一分为二，生物学便借这个词指细胞分裂。

senses.title: A split within a group
senses.definition: a division of an organization or group into separate parts
senses.definitionCN: 组织或团体分成若干独立的部分
senses.example: The fission of the party into rival factions shocked its members.
senses.exampleCN: 该党分裂成相互竞争的派系，令党员震惊。
senses.why: People borrow the physical split to describe a group that no longer holds together.
senses.whyCN: 人们借用物理上的裂开来形容不再团结的团体。

senses.title: To split by fission
senses.definition: to divide, or cause something to divide, by fission
senses.definitionCN: 通过裂变而分开，或使某物发生裂变
senses.example: The nucleus fissions when it absorbs a slow neutron.
senses.exampleCN: 原子核吸收慢中子后发生裂变。
senses.why: English turns many nouns into verbs, so the process can also be stated as an action.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把名词转为动词，于是这一过程也可以说成一个动作。

intro.en: Fission comes from Latin fissio, a splitting, from the verb findere, to split, whose past participle is fissus.
intro.cn: fission 来自拉丁语 fissio（裂开），源于动词 findere（劈开），其过去分词是 fissus。

items.en: Findere means to split or cleave.
items.cn: findere 意为劈开、分裂。

items.en: Fissio names a splitting or division.
items.cn: fissio 意为裂开、分裂。

items.en: Fissus is the past participle of findere.
items.cn: fissus 是 findere 的过去分词。

items.en: Fission enters English as a learned word for splitting.
items.cn: 十七世纪，fission 作为表示「分裂」的书面词进入英语。

items.en: Physicists adopt fission for the splitting of uranium nuclei.
items.cn: 一九三九年，物理学家用 fission 指铀原子核的分裂。

items.en: Biology and politics extend fission to cells and to groups of people.
items.cn: 生物学和政治领域把 fission 扩展到细胞与人群团体。

note.en: Fission shares the Latin splitting root with fissure and fissile, and sits near split and division.
note.cn: fission 与 fissure、fissile 共享拉丁语「劈开」词根，并与 split、division 意义相邻。

entries.definition: a long narrow crack in rock or tissue
entries.definitionCN: 岩石或组织上的细长裂缝

entries.definition: able to undergo nuclear fission
capable of being split by fission
to divide into parts
the act of separating into parts
the splitting of a cell or a crystal

normalIntro.en: Fission is Latin splitting: one thing becomes two, whether nucleus, cell, or group.
normalIntro.cn: fission 是拉丁语的「劈开」：一个东西变成两个，无论原子核、细胞还是团体。

normal.en: Findere, the Latin verb to split, hides inside fission.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词 findere（劈开）就藏在 fission 里。

normal.en: Nuclear fission powers reactors and also makes bombs.
normal.cn: 核裂变既能驱动反应堆，也能制造炸弹。

normal.en: Fission products are the smaller nuclei left after a split.
normal.cn: 「fission products」是分裂后留下的较小原子核。

normal.en: A cell that divides by fission simply becomes two cells.
normal.cn: 通过分裂繁殖的细胞直接变成两个细胞。

normal.en: Compare fusion: fission splits apart, fusion joins together.
normal.cn: 对比 fusion：fission 是分裂，fusion 是合并。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy ball struck by a tiny pellet, breaking into two glowing halves.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗沉重的大球被小颗粒击中，裂成两个发亮的半块。

abstract.en: Picture one soft cell pinching itself into two identical cells.
abstract.cn: 想象一个柔软的细胞把自己捏成两个一样的细胞。

abstract.en: Picture one club splitting into two rival clubs overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个俱乐部一夜之间分成两个对立的俱乐部。

examples.en: Nuclear fission releases far more energy than burning coal.
examples.cn: 核裂变释放的能量远多于燃烧煤炭。

examples.en: Some bacteria divide by fission every twenty minutes.
examples.cn: 有些细菌每二十分钟分裂一次。

examples.en: The discovery of fission changed the course of history.
examples.cn: 裂变的发现改变了历史进程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费申」——原子核一分为二，工程师就要费神控制能量；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 findere（劈开）→ 过去分词 fissus → 名词 fissio（裂开）→ 英语 fission，核心义「一分为二」。

sensesIntro.en: Fission moves from the nucleus to the cell, then to groups of people, and finally to the verb that names the splitting.
sensesIntro.cn: fission 从原子核移到细胞，再移到人群团体，最后转为动词，指「使裂变」这一动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy nucleus breaking into two glowing halves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗重原子核裂成两个发亮的半块。

branches.en: Nuclear splitting is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 核裂变是现代最主要的义项。

branches.en: The process and the verb name the same splitting from two angles.
branches.cn: 过程与动词从两个角度命名同一种分裂。

branches.en: A cell splitting into two is the biological sense.
branches.cn: 细胞一分为二是生物学义项。

branches.en: A group breaking apart borrows the physical image.
branches.cn: 团体分崩离析借用了物理上的意象。

branches.en: Both a cell and a group can divide into separate parts.
branches.cn: 细胞与团体都能分成各自独立的部分。

intro.en: Fission is built from the Latin verb findere and the noun fissio, and English -ion and -able form its family.
intro.cn: fission 由拉丁动词 findere 与名词 fissio 构成，英语的 -ion 与 -able 又组成它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Findere means to split; fissio and fissus come from the same verb and carry the same image.
latinIntro.cn: findere 意为劈开；fissio 与 fissus 出自同一动词，承载同一意象。

items.example: Findere supplies the splitting image behind fission.
items.exampleCN: findere 提供 fission 背后的分裂意象。

items.example: Fissio is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: fissio 是这一英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: Fissus is the past participle of findere.
items.exampleCN: fissus 是 findere 的过去分词。

items.meaning: a splitting of a nucleus or cell
items.example: Fission keeps the Latin noun sense.
items.exampleCN: fission 保留了拉丁名词的含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或其结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion turns fissio into an English noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 把 fissio 变成英语名词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms fissionable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 fissionable。

items.example: Fissile shares the same Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: fissile 共享同一拉丁词干。

items.example: Fissure keeps the concrete image of a split.
items.exampleCN: fissure 保留「裂开」的具体意象。

items.example: The suffix -able marks capability.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 表示能力。

definition_zh: 断断续续的；一阵一阵的；不规则的
definition_en: stopping and starting irregularly, rather than continuing steadily
core_image: 夜里一盏忽明忽暗的灯，亮一下又暗一下
scene: 夜里风势忽大忽小，他睡得极不安稳，一会儿醒一会儿又睡。He had a fitful sleep as the wind rose and fell.
sceneCN: 这里 fitful 是「断断续续的」（第 1 个义项：时停时续、不连贯）；句意：风势起伏，他的睡眠断断续续。

pos.zh: 断断续续的；一阵一阵的；不规则的

derivatives.zh: fitful 加 -ly 构成，指断断续续地、一阵一阵地
fitful 加 -ness 构成，指断续无常的状态

senses.title: Stopping and starting
senses.definition: happening for short periods with pauses in between
senses.definitionCN: 持续很短一段时间，中间带有停顿
senses.example: She finally fell into a fitful sleep before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前她终于进入断断续续的睡眠。
senses.why: Fit names a sudden attack or bout, and -ful means full of them, so fitful is full of starts and stops.
senses.whyCN: fit 指突然的一阵发作，-ful 意为「充满」，所以 fitful 就是充满一阵一阵的起落。

senses.title: Blowing in sudden bursts
senses.definition: coming in short, uneven bursts, as wind or rain does
senses.definitionCN: 像风或雨那样一阵阵不均匀地到来
senses.example: Fitful gusts rattled the shutters all night.
senses.exampleCN: 阵阵狂风整夜摇着百叶窗。
senses.why: A bout of wind is a fit of wind, so the same image covers weather that cannot hold a steady force.
senses.whyCN: 一阵风就是风的一「阵」，同一个意象也覆盖无法保持稳定力度的天气。

senses.title: Uneven in progress
senses.definition: not steady or reliable, with periods of success and failure
senses.definitionCN: 不稳定、不可靠，成功与失败交替出现
senses.example: The project made fitful progress through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目在冬天进展时断时续。
senses.why: Anything that advances in fits looks unreliable, so the word describes uneven effort and results.
senses.whyCN: 凡是一阵一阵前进的事物都显得不可靠，于是这个词也形容起伏不定的努力与结果。

senses.title: Changing in mood
senses.definition: marked by sudden changes of mood or by restlessness
senses.definitionCN: 情绪突然变化或坐立不安的
senses.example: He was in a fitful mood and could not settle to anything.
senses.exampleCN: 他情绪不定，什么事都静不下心做。
senses.why: A fit of emotion is another kind of attack, so a fitful person is ruled by sudden surges of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 情绪的「一阵」也是一种发作，所以 fitful 的人会被突然涌起的情感支配。

senses.title: Flashing unevenly
senses.definition: shining or sounding in irregular flashes rather than steadily
senses.definitionCN: 以不规则的闪烁或声响出现，而非稳定持续
senses.example: A fitful light flickered behind the curtains.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘后面有一道忽明忽暗的光。
senses.why: Light that appears in fits copies the same pattern of short bursts separated by gaps.
senses.whyCN: 以「一阵一阵」方式出现的光，重复了同样「短促爆发加间隔」的模式。

intro.en: Fitful is a native English formation from fit, an old noun for a seizure, plus the suffix -ful.
intro.cn: fitful 是英语本土构词，由古名词 fit（发作）加后缀 -ful 构成。

items.en: Fit names a seizure or a sudden attack of illness.
items.cn: fit 指疾病的发作或突然的一阵。

items.en: Fit keeps the sense of a bout or a short period of activity.
items.cn: 中古英语 fit 保留「一阵发作或一小段时间活动」的含义。

items.en: The suffix -ful is added, giving fitful, meaning marked by fits.
items.cn: 十八世纪加上后缀 -ful，构成 fitful，意为「由一阵阵发作构成的」。

items.en: Writers extend fitful to sleep, wind, progress and mood.
items.cn: 十九世纪，作家把 fitful 扩展到睡眠、风、进展与情绪。

items.en: Fitful now describes anything that starts and stops unevenly.
items.cn: 现代英语中，fitful 形容任何断续而不均匀的事物。

note.en: Fitful comes from fit, a seizure, not from fit meaning suitable, and it sits near intermittent and erratic.
note.cn: fitful 来自表示「发作」的 fit，而不是表示「合适」的 fit；它与 intermittent、erratic 意义相近。

entries.definition: a sudden attack or bout
in a suitable manner
entries.definitionCN: 适当地；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: right or appropriate
entries.definitionCN: 合适的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: stopping and starting at intervals
happening at irregular intervals
unpredictable and uneven

normalIntro.en: Fitful is fit plus -ful: full of fits, full of sudden starts and stops.
normalIntro.cn: fitful 是 fit 加 -ful：充满一阵阵发作，也就是充满突然的起落。

normal.en: Fit here means a bout or a seizure, not a good match.
normal.cn: 这里的 fit 指一阵发作，而不是「合适」。

normal.en: A fitful sleep is broken by many short waking moments.
normal.cn: 「fitful sleep」被许多短暂的清醒时刻打断。

normal.en: Fitful gusts come in bursts instead of a steady wind.
normal.cn: 「fitful gusts」一阵阵出现，而不是稳定地吹。

normal.en: Fitful progress looks like two steps forward and one back.
normal.cn: 「fitful progress」就像进两步、退一步。

normal.en: Fitfully is the adverb, and fitfulness the noun.
normal.cn: fitfully 是副词，fitfulness 是名词。

abstract.en: Picture a sleeper waking, dozing, and waking again before dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在天亮前醒了又睡、睡了又醒。

abstract.en: Picture a flag snapping in bursts of wind, then going limp.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗被一阵阵风扯动，随后又软下来。

abstract.en: Picture a graph that rises, stalls, and rises again.
abstract.cn: 想象一条曲线上升、停住、再上升。

examples.en: His fitful sleep left him tired in the morning.
examples.cn: 他断断续续的睡眠让他在早上很疲惫。

examples.en: Fitful rain showers continued through the afternoon.
examples.cn: 阵雨断断续续下了一下午。

examples.en: The team made fitful progress on the report.
examples.cn: 团队在报告上进展时断时续。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费特福」——睡眠断断续续，一会儿醒一会儿睡，真费神；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fit（疾病的发作、一阵）+ -ful（充满……的）→ fitful，核心义「一阵一阵发作的」。

sensesIntro.en: Fitful begins with the idea of a seizure or a bout, then covers weather, progress and mood, and finally any uneven flashing.
sensesIntro.cn: fitful 从「发作、一阵」的观念出发，继而覆盖天气、进展与情绪，最后指任何不均匀的闪动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp that brightens and dims without a steady glow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏没有稳定亮度、忽明忽暗的灯。

branches.en: Broken sleep is the everyday fitful experience.
branches.cn: 断断续续的睡眠是 fitful 最日常的用法。

branches.en: Wind in sudden bursts repeats the fit pattern outdoors.
branches.cn: 风的一阵阵发作把「一阵」模式搬到户外。

branches.en: Uneven progress shows fits of effort separated by pauses.
branches.cn: 进展起伏表现为努力的一阵与停顿交替。

branches.en: Mood swings are fits of feeling.
branches.cn: 情绪起伏就是情感的一阵阵发作。

branches.en: A flashing light is a visual burst with gaps between.
branches.cn: 闪动的光就是带间隔的视觉爆发。

intro.en: Fitful is a native English formation: the old noun fit plus the suffix -ful.
intro.cn: fitful 是英语本土构词：古名词 fit 加后缀 -ful。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin root; its base fit is Germanic, so no Latin cognates are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，词基 fit 属日耳曼语，因此没有记录拉丁同源词。

items.example: Fit is the old noun behind fitful.
items.exampleCN: fit 是 fitful 背后的古名词。

items.example: The suffix -ful means full of something.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 意为充满某物。

items.example: Fitful joins fit and -ful.
items.exampleCN: fitful 由 fit 与 -ful 结合而成。

items.example: Fitfully adds -ly to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: fitfully 在形容词后加 -ly。

items.example: Fitfulness adds -ness to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: fitfulness 在形容词后加 -ness。

items.example: Fitting comes from fit meaning to suit, a different root.
items.exampleCN: fitting 来自表示「适合」的 fit，是另一条词源。

items.example: Fitly also belongs to the suitable fit.
items.exampleCN: fitly 同样属于表示「合适」的 fit。

items.example: Unfit is un- plus fit meaning suitable.
items.exampleCN: unfit 是 un- 加表示「合适」的 fit。

definition_zh: 固定设施；固定成员；体育赛事
definition_en: an object fixed in place, a person or thing always present, or a scheduled sports match
core_image: 浴室里焊死在墙上的那排架子，搬不走也换不掉
scene: 老球迷每个赛季都坐同一个座位，这场主场比赛早已排进赛程。The home fixture had been printed in the schedule weeks before.
sceneCN: 这里 fixture 是「体育赛事」（第 3 个义项：按日期安排的一场比赛）；句意：这场主场比赛早在几周前就排进了赛程。

pos.zh: 固定设施；固定成员；体育赛事

derivatives.zh: fixture 的词基，指固定、安装或修理
fix 加 -ation 构成，指固定的行为，也指执念
fix 加 -ity 构成，指固定不变的性质

senses.title: An item fixed in place
senses.definition: an object attached to a building or position so that it cannot easily be moved
senses.definitionCN: 固定在建筑物或位置上、不易移动的物件
senses.example: The bathroom came with a new light fixture.
senses.exampleCN: 浴室配了一盏新的灯具。
senses.why: The Latin root means to fasten, and -ure names the result, so a fixture is something fastened down.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「固定」，-ure 表示结果，所以 fixture 就是被固定住的东西。

senses.title: A regular presence
senses.definition: a person or thing that is always found in a place or situation
senses.definitionCN: 总能在某地或某种场合见到的人或事物
senses.example: The old coach is a fixture at every home game.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老教练是每场主场比赛的常客。
senses.why: Something fastened in place stays there, and people use the same image for a familiar presence.
senses.whyCN: 固定住的东西会一直留在原处，人们便用同一意象指熟悉而常在的人或物。

senses.title: A scheduled sports event
senses.definition: a sports match arranged for a particular date
senses.definitionCN: 安排在特定日期举行的一场体育比赛
senses.example: The next fixture is against the league leaders.
senses.exampleCN: 下一场比赛的对手是联赛领头羊。
senses.why: British clubs fixed their matches in advance, and the dated match took the name of the fixed arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 英国俱乐部提前把比赛日期定下来，这场定好日期的比赛就沿用了「固定安排」的名称。

senses.title: The act of fixing
senses.definition: the act or process of fastening something in position
senses.definitionCN: 把某物固定到某个位置的行为或过程
senses.example: The fixture of the shelves took the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 安装这些架子花了一整个下午。
senses.why: The noun can name the action behind the result, not only the object that results.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能指结果，也能指产生结果的动作，所以 fixture 也可指固定、安装。

senses.title: A work-holding device
senses.definition: a device that holds a workpiece steady during machining
senses.definitionCN: 机械加工时把工件固定住的装置
senses.example: The machinist clamped the block into a sturdy fixture.
senses.exampleCN: 机械师把方块夹进一个结实的夹具。
senses.why: Manufacturing borrows the word for the tool that fastens the work, keeping the core image of fixing.
senses.whyCN: 制造业借这个词指固定工件的工具，保留了「固定」的核心意象。

senses.title: Property attached to land
senses.definition: in law, an item of property so attached to land that it is treated as part of it
senses.definitionCN: 法律上附着于土地、被视为土地一部分的财产
senses.example: The court treated the greenhouse as a fixture of the land.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把这间温室视为土地的附属物。
senses.why: Law pushes physical attachment to its limit: what is fixed to the land belongs to the land.
senses.whyCN: 法律把物理上的附着推到极限：固定在土地上的东西就归土地所有。

intro.en: Fixture is an English noun formed from the Latin-rooted verb fix plus the suffix -ure, perhaps after Late Latin fixura.
intro.cn: fixture 是英语名词，由拉丁词根的动词 fix 加后缀 -ure 构成，可能受到晚期拉丁语 fixura 的影响。

items.en: Figere means to fasten or fix.
items.cn: figere 意为固定、钉住。

items.en: Fixus is the past participle, meaning fastened.
items.cn: fixus 是过去分词，意为已被固定。

items.en: English forms fixture from fix with the suffix -ure.
items.cn: 十七世纪，英语用 fix 加后缀 -ure 构成 fixture。

items.en: The word names installed household fittings and scheduled matches.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这个词既指安装好的家用设备，也指定好日期的比赛。

items.en: Law and engineering add attached property and work-holding devices.
items.cn: 现代英语在法律与工程领域增加了附属物与夹具的含义。

note.en: Fixture comes from the Latin verb for fixing, and it sits near fitting, appliance and installation.
note.cn: fixture 来自表示「固定」的拉丁动词，与 fitting、appliance、installation 意义相邻。

entries.definition: to fasten or repair
the act of fixing, or an obsession
fastened or unchanging
a small part fixed into a building
entries.definitionCN: 固定在建筑物上的小配件

entries.definition: a machine used in the home
equipment set up in place

normalIntro.en: Fixture is fix plus -ure: the thing that has been fixed, and the act of fixing it.
normalIntro.cn: fixture 是 fix 加 -ure：被固定住的东西，以及固定的动作。

normal.en: Fix is the verb, and -ure turns it into a noun.
normal.cn: fix 是动词，-ure 使它变成名词。

normal.en: A light fixture is fixed to the ceiling and stays there.
normal.cn: 「light fixture」固定在天花板上，留在那里。

normal.en: A fixture list tells fans when each match will be played.
normal.cn: 「fixture list」告诉球迷每场比赛何时进行。

normal.en: A person can be a fixture at a club, always present.
normal.cn: 一个人也可以是俱乐部的常客，总在那里。

normal.en: Compare fixture with fitting: both are fixed, but a fitting is usually smaller.
normal.cn: 对比 fixture 与 fitting：两者都是固定的，但 fitting 通常更小。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy shelf bolted to a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个沉重的架子用螺栓固定在墙上。

abstract.en: Picture the same face in the same seat every week.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张面孔每星期都坐在同一个座位。

abstract.en: Picture a printed match list pinned to a club door.
abstract.cn: 想象一张印好的比赛列表钉在俱乐部的大门上。

examples.en: The kitchen fixtures were replaced during the renovation.
examples.cn: 装修时厨房的固定设施被换掉了。

examples.en: She has become a fixture at the local library.
examples.cn: 她已成了当地图书馆的常客。

examples.en: The weekend fixture attracted a full stadium.
examples.cn: 周末的赛事坐满了体育场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费克斯彻」——想象工人把架子固定在墙上，怎么推都不动；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 figere（固定、钉住）→ 过去分词 fixus → 英语 fix 加 -ure → fixture，核心义「被固定住的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Fixture starts as the result of fixing, then names an installed object, a familiar presence, a dated match, and finally legal and engineering attachments.
sensesIntro.cn: fixture 从「固定的结果」出发，继而指安装好的物件、熟悉常在的人、定好日期的比赛，最后指法律与工程上的附着物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shelf bolted to a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：用螺栓固定在墙上的架子。

branches.en: An installed object is the concrete base sense.
branches.cn: 安装好的物件是具体的基底义项。

branches.en: A familiar presence is a person treated like a fixed object.
branches.cn: 熟悉常在的人被当作固定之物来称呼。

branches.en: A dated match is an arrangement fixed in advance.
branches.cn: 定好日期的比赛就是提前固定下来的安排。

branches.en: The action of fixing and the tool that fastens share the same image.
branches.cn: 固定的动作与固定工件的工具共享同一意象。

branches.en: Physical attachment and legal attachment are two degrees of the same idea.
branches.cn: 物理附着与法律附着是同一观念的两个程度。

intro.en: Fixture is a Latin-rooted English noun built on fix, with -ure and a wide technical family.
intro.cn: fixture 是拉丁词根的英语名词，以 fix 为基础加 -ure，并带出一整族技术用语。

latinIntro.en: Latin figere means to fasten, and its participle fixus gives the stem fix-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 figere 意为固定，其过去分词 fixus 提供词干 fix-。

items.example: Figere supplies the fastening image.
items.exampleCN: figere 提供「固定」的意象。

items.example: Fixus is the past participle of figere.
items.exampleCN: fixus 是 figere 的过去分词。

items.example: Fix is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: fix 是整个词族的词基。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或其结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ure forms a noun of result.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ure 构成表示结果的名词。

items.example: Fixture keeps the result sense.
items.exampleCN: fixture 保留「结果」的含义。

items.meaningCN: 固定设施或赛事的复数
items.example: Fixtures is the plural of fixture.
items.exampleCN: fixtures 是 fixture 的复数。

items.meaning: the act of fixing, or an obsession
items.example: Fixation adds -ation to fix.
items.exampleCN: fixation 在 fix 后加 -ation。

items.example: Fixity adds -ity to fix.
items.exampleCN: fixity 在 fix 后加 -ity。

items.example: Fixative adds -ative to fix.
items.exampleCN: fixative 在 fix 后加 -ative。

items.example: Fixed adds -ed to the verb.
items.exampleCN: fixed 在动词后加 -ed。
